S01.title: Top of the Ladder
S01.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I raise a finger before anyone speaks.
beats.text: You may begin when I lower this finger. Bring the blue folder to me for approval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only a lunch menu.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And it's reached the correct level of decision-making.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I take the chair at the head of the table.
beats.text: I'll decide when we're finished. Bring the blue folder to me for approval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I sit at the head instead?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once I've approved what you intend to do with the head.

S02.title: Borrowed Authority
S02.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I straighten my badge, then offer my chair.
beats.text: I'd like this to remain voluntary. Back me up when I announce the new schedule. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why would I back you up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because otherwise this badge is a very lonely piece of plastic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I uncross my arms and set out another cup.
beats.text: I'm still in charge, provided we're all happy. Back me up when I announce the new schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we change the schedule?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A small change demonstrates how firmly I'm leading by agreement.

S03.title: The Only Professional
S03.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the instructions right side up.
beats.text: Let's try this the trained way. Use the labelled tray instead of the floor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just a paperclip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A simple object handled with avoidable incompetence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put on gloves to handle a single paperclip.
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Use the labelled tray instead of the floor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That tray looks like the others.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To an untrained eye, yes. Notice my beautifully patient voice.

S04.title: Act Like You Belong
S04.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I copy the hand gesture a beat late.
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Point to where the experienced people sign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The experienced people don't sign.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I was checking whether you'd catch that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn my form over when you turn yours.
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Point to where the experienced people sign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've never been here before.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not in this exact arrangement. They've moved all the familiar confusion.

S05.title: The Protégé Problem
S05.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I correct the angle of the pen I offered.
beats.text: Better. That's almost how I taught you. Let me check your opening sentence before you read it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You taught me when I was six.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A crucial year. Most of your improvement happened after my intervention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set my old instruction sheet beside yours.
beats.text: You've come so far since my first lesson. Let me check your opening sentence before you read it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote the entire speech myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And look how well you still arrange words in the order I introduced.

S06.title: Hidden Power
S06.instruction: Act publicly modest while making choices as though you control the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I quietly move the only key into my pocket.
beats.text: No need to put me in charge. Pass the final version by me before sending it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why do you need the final version?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just so nobody wastes time making a decision I'll need to undo.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave the approval box blank and smile.
beats.text: I'm merely helping. Pass the final version by me before sending it. Then I'll sign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've already agreed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I'll let you know whether that changes anything.

S07.title: Before They Were Impressive
S07.instruction: Treat another player with old familiarity. Casually puncture formality, grandeur, or attempts to impress you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I brush imaginary crumbs from your grand chair.
beats.text: Still the same old seat-stealer. Let me call you by the old nickname today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please use my new title.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right, Your Sandwich Thief. Does that go on the programme?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I address the gold nameplate instead of your face.
beats.text: Fancy plate, same person who ate my sandwiches. Let me call you by the old nickname today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That nickname isn't appropriate now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Neither were the crumbs in my bed. We both survived a little informality.

S08.title: You Owe Me
S08.instruction: Behave as though another person's success is partly yours. Refer to favors, sacrifices, or guidance as if the debt is obvious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place my faded receipt beside your new certificate.
beats.text: My bus fare got you to that first interview. Leave a little room for my name in your thank-you speech.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are several people to thank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Start with the one who paid for you to meet the others.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I straighten the certificate I once paid to frame.
beats.text: We both know whose shoulders got you here. Leave a little room for my name in your thank-you speech.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was one bus fare.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With an extraordinary return on my emotional investment.

S09.title: The Responsible One
S09.instruction: Take responsibility for everyone and everything. Fix problems before anyone asks, then resent having to do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I collect the abandoned cups while still talking.
beats.text: Already taken care of, apparently by me again. Tell me which of these jobs you'll remember tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can make my own lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I've packed the ingredients to make remembering easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put down a spare key and a packed lunch.
beats.text: I remembered for both of us. Tell me which of these jobs you'll remember tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't have to do all this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why was everything so relieved when I arrived?

S10.title: Old Rivals
S10.instruction: Choose another player as your measuring stick. Compare achievements, score small victories, and refuse to be outdone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I measure my pile against yours with a ruler.
beats.text: Mine's taller by three millimetres. Show me how fast you can fold the next towel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not racing you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my lead should remain pleasantly uncontested.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add a tally beside my name.
beats.text: That's one to me. Show me how fast you can fold the next towel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a towel, not a sport.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You'd say that with those corners.

S11.title: Only You
S11.instruction: Choose one person as the only one you trust. Seek their help while hiding how much you depend on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw my chair close to yours, away from the others.
beats.text: I'm asking you, not the room. Tell me whether the door is safe to open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ask someone else about the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I could. I'd just ask you afterward whether their answer was safe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pass you my notes folded into a tiny square.
beats.text: I could do this alone. Just read these first. Tell me whether the door is safe to open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can read your own notes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm comparing two expert opinions. Yours and the one I'll have after yours.

S12.title: After What Happened
S12.instruction: Carry yourself as if an unnamed past incident still hangs over the interaction. Read ordinary remarks through that memory.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stop with my hand above an ordinary teacup.
beats.text: That cup. After last time, really? Explain why you put that particular cup out again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only clean cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what you said the first time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave one empty place untouched.
beats.text: Let's not pretend this is just another dinner. Explain why you put that particular cup out again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happened with that cup?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting how clean your memory has become.

S13.title: Envious Admiration
S13.instruction: Be sincerely impressed by another player while trying not to appear lesser. Compliment, imitate, and compete at the same time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I copy your relaxed pose too carefully.
beats.text: That looks effortless on you. Mine takes discipline. Watch my version before deciding which was better.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't have to copy me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not copying. I'm establishing an improved reference version.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I applaud, then demonstrate the same flourish.
beats.text: Beautiful. I've made one tiny improvement. Watch my version before deciding which was better.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Both versions were nice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine required more discipline. Surely that makes nice worth more.

S14.title: The Old You
S14.instruction: Perform the person you used to be, even when that identity no longer fits. Defend the old version of yourself whenever it is challenged.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I dust off my old stage jacket.
beats.text: The sleeves still fit the person I am. Introduce me with the nickname on this jacket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody knows that nickname.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tonight they'll meet the person worth knowing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I sign with the nickname I used twenty years ago.
beats.text: I haven't retired that name. Introduce me with the nickname on this jacket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The jacket is twenty years old.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And it still understands exactly who should be inside it.

S15.title: Replacement Fear
S15.instruction: Behave as if your place is insecure. Make yourself indispensable and treat small changes as threats.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move a new nameplate away from my desk.
beats.text: Just making room for the person who already works here. Let me handle the keys for another week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new person needs a desk too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They can use any desk that doesn't imply I was optional.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pin up a list of jobs only I remember.
beats.text: Replacing me would mean replacing all of this. Let me handle the keys for another week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're only spare keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Spare to a newcomer. Essential to the person who knows every lock.

S16.title: For Their Own Good
S16.instruction: Take charge of another person's choices because you trust your judgment more than theirs. Frame control as care.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide the sharper scissors out of reach.
beats.text: I'll choose the safe option for both of us. Choose the option I left uncovered.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd prefer the other option.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the part of your judgement I'm protecting you from.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover two choices on the menu with my hand.
beats.text: I'm protecting you from an expensive mistake. Choose the option I left uncovered.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You covered the thing I wanted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Care can be very efficient when it arrives before choice.

S17.title: Their Opinion Matters
S17.instruction: Seek one person's approval while pretending their opinion is irrelevant. Adjust yourself whenever they respond.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I adjust my collar while watching your face.
beats.text: Not that it matters to me. Say whether the blue shirt makes the right impression.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The blue shirt was fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was? I'll change back. Not because you said anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I change the seating plan after glancing at you.
beats.text: Better? Purely a practical question. Say whether the blue shirt makes the right impression.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever makes you comfortable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd be comfortable with a slightly more definite endorsement.

S18.title: Fishing for Praise
S18.instruction: You desperately want praise but refuse to ask for it. Create opportunities for others to notice your greatness.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave my finished puzzle directly under the lamp.
beats.text: Oh, that? Only took me all night. Take a closer look at the piece nobody else could solve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a very big puzzle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the unsolvable section is mine. Take your time noticing it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pause beside my trophy with a polishing cloth.
beats.text: Don't let me interrupt your appreciation. Take a closer look at the piece nobody else could solve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Didn't you win that last year?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Remarkably, the achievement has maintained its quality.

S19.title: Sacred Procedure
S19.instruction: Treat an ordinary activity as a solemn ritual. Protect every step, object, and tradition from casual interference.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the teaspoon exactly three times.
beats.text: We finish the third turn before speaking. Hold the plate level while I complete the final turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just put the plate down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not before the biscuit has completed its entrance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place a napkin beneath the ceremonial biscuit.
beats.text: The biscuit never touches bare wood. Hold the plate level while I complete the final turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why must it be level?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because last time somebody called this merely a snack.

S20.title: Red Alert
S20.instruction: Treat every development as urgent evidence of a crisis. Escalate precautions faster than the facts justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I mark an exit route around one spilled drop.
beats.text: This is how the big disasters start. Help me move the cups away from the danger zone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's one drop of water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One visible drop. I've marked where the invisible ones might spread.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pack a torch after hearing a chair squeak.
beats.text: We may have seconds, not minutes. Help me move the cups away from the danger zone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chair squeaked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we have an auditory warning as well. Take the torch.

S21.title: Cause for Celebration
S21.instruction: Interpret every development as a reason to celebrate. Find victory in setbacks, warnings, and bad news.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I make a toast with the empty jug.
beats.text: Wonderful, we've eliminated the washing-up problem. Raise a glass to our unexpected new opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: But the jug is empty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we can toast twice without spilling a drop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I clap over a torn invitation.
beats.text: Now we can invite twice as many people. Raise a glass to our unexpected new opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We tore the only invitation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now two people can arrive carrying proof.

S22.title: Practical Realist
S22.instruction: Accept any unusual premise without debate. Focus immediately on schedules, costs, safety, and what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I write a cost beside the words 'talking ceiling'.
beats.text: Fine, the ceiling talks. Who pays its overtime? Tell me who's cleaning up when it finishes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not surprised it talks?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll be surprised if its wages fit the maintenance budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the miraculous object on a labelled tray.
beats.text: Miracles still need somewhere to drip. Tell me who's cleaning up when it finishes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a miracle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the miracle is dripping on a borrowed carpet. Who signs for cleaning?

S23.title: The Important Thing
S23.instruction: Choose one ordinary object, phrase, or rule and treat it as vitally important. Keep bringing the scene back to it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I centre a paperclip while ignoring the larger mess.
beats.text: Everything else can wait until this is straight. Put that paperclip back exactly where it was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The room is full of rubbish.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And that rubbish nearly swallowed our last straight paperclip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pick the same paperclip out of a rubbish bag.
beats.text: You nearly threw away the essential part. Put that paperclip back exactly where it was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we discuss the missing roof?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the paperclip. I'd like one dependable structure in this building.

S24.title: The Grand Design
S24.instruction: Treat coincidences and interruptions as parts of a larger plan. Connect everything with absolute conviction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I connect two coffee rings on a scrap of paper.
beats.text: Two circles. Two cancellations. It's all arranged. Put the next coincidence on this map with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those are marks from our cups.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Something knew where we'd sit before we knew what to discuss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add the ringing phone to my diagram.
beats.text: Even the interruption was scheduled by something bigger. Put the next coincidence on this map with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The phone rings every day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the plan has been rehearsing this interruption for years.

S25.title: Default Decision-Maker
S25.instruction: Take charge of every small practical choice, treating speed and efficiency as proof that you should remain in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I sort the lunch orders before finishing my sentence.
beats.text: Blue slips first. Decided. We've saved a minute. Put the sandwiches in the order I've marked.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I choose my own sandwich?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After I've arranged the decision efficiently for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I start stacking chairs while announcing the plan.
beats.text: I'm quickest, so I'll choose the order. Put the sandwiches in the order I've marked.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We haven't agreed on the order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've completed three chairs while discussing agreement. My system works.

S26.title: Temporary Authority
S26.instruction: Project brisk confidence through the routine, as though any hesitation would reveal that your authority is only temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hide the word 'temporary' on my badge.
beats.text: We have a very established system this afternoon. Bring the deliveries through this door until five.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're only covering for lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A period that requires exceptionally concentrated leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I consult a clock before asserting the rule.
beats.text: While I'm covering this desk, Bring the deliveries through this door until five.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who put you in charge?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone currently eating. Let's not interrupt governance with sandwiches.

S27.title: There’s a Right Way
S27.instruction: Correct how ordinary tasks are done, emphasizing tiny standards that only a true professional would notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn every mug handle to the same angle.
beats.text: There's a correct way to leave a handle. Fold the loose corner under before stacking it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does the corner matter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not until every towel collapses into amateur triangles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I examine a folded towel at eye level.
beats.text: That corner isn't finished; it's surrendered. Fold the loose corner under before stacking it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We only use them to dry things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And professionals can dry things without surrendering their standards.

S28.title: Regular Around Here
S28.instruction: Act like a longtime insider by recognizing routines, offering shortcuts, and treating unfamiliar details as recent changes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I use the side entrance and wave familiarly.
beats.text: They must have moved the bell since my last visit. Show me where they've moved my usual mug.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've never kept a mug for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ah, the new storage policy. Very different from my usual arrangement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point confidently at the wrong coat hook.
beats.text: Ah, redecorated again. Show me where they've moved my usual mug.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That hook belongs to the owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, they always did favour my side of the wall.

S29.title: Let Me Show You
S29.instruction: Turn each simple task into a lesson. Demonstrate, supervise, and correct as though experience has made you indispensable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I fold one corner slowly for inspection.
beats.text: Watch the wrist. You'll thank me later. Copy this knot once before I let go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already know the knot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can appreciate the demonstration on a deeper level.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stop halfway through a familiar knot.
beats.text: This is the part beginners rush. Copy this knot once before I let go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a simple fold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The finest opportunity to learn how complex your mistakes could be.

S30.title: Keeper of the Details
S30.instruction: Act outwardly helpful while controlling the small information, supplies, or access everyone needs to proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep the spare batteries in my closed palm.
beats.text: Happy to help once the details are settled. Bring the shopping list to me before opening the cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can buy batteries elsewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I also have the address of the shop that's open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the supply cupboard key on a string.
beats.text: I'm just looking after the little things. Bring the shopping list to me before opening the cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why do you need the list?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So I know which shelf to make available first.

S31.title: Same Old Routine
S31.instruction: Use familiar shorthand and old habits immediately, as though past routines still govern the present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set out two cups without asking.
beats.text: Your chipped one, my ugly one. Same as always. Take the drying side like we used to.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We don't use that signal anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our hands apparently missed the announcement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I start the old hand signal over the washing-up.
beats.text: You know this signal. Take the drying side like we used to.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I usually wash now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I usually know which cup you'd reach for. Let's find the old rhythm.

S32.title: One More Favor
S32.instruction: Treat every small request as part of a long-running balance sheet of favors, inconveniences, and repayments.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add a tiny stroke to my favour notebook.
beats.text: That's the third lift this month. Cover my trip home this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was only a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: In rain, on Tuesday, with my heater broken. I've indexed the details.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn to the page labelled 'rainy Tuesdays'.
beats.text: I did keep the receipts for my kindness. Cover my trip home this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said not to mention it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I meant in public. My private accounts remain admirably complete.

S33.title: The Designated Reminder
S33.instruction: Keep track of what everyone was supposed to remember. Supply reminders before being asked and treat forgetfulness as your familiar burden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pin a reminder to the reminder.
beats.text: I remembered that you'd forget this one. Set your own alarm for tomorrow's delivery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I set my own reminder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I've set one to check whether yours went off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer the umbrella from my bag with a sigh.
beats.text: Forecast was on the note I left. Set your own alarm for tomorrow's delivery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I knew it would rain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then explain why my umbrella is doing the remembering for both of us.

S34.title: Keeping Score
S34.instruction: Treat arrival times, effort, memory, and sacrifice as a running score you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I time my washing-up with a kitchen timer.
beats.text: Four minutes. How long was yours again? Count how many stairs I carried these up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your bags happened to be heavier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A remarkable coincidence every time I'm being generous.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I weigh the two shopping bags before taking one.
beats.text: My half weighs more, as usual. Count how many stairs I carried these up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did my share too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's count the stairs before deciding what share means.

S35.title: You Know the System
S35.instruction: Use another person’s knowledge of the routine while pretending you could manage perfectly well alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hand you the unfamiliar keyring casually.
beats.text: Just checking that you remember the route. Point me toward the right counter without making a fuss.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't know where we're going.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know the general concept of arriving. Confirm the small turns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold a blank form behind your completed one.
beats.text: I'm comparing layouts, not copying. Point me toward the right counter without making a fuss.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're copying my form.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Comparing. Copying would involve admitting mine was blank first.

S36.title: Still About Last Time
S36.instruction: Treat each minor inconvenience as confirmation of an older grievance and the same recurring problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stop beside a single abandoned sock.
beats.text: Different sock, same conversation. Tell me what's different from the last promised cleanup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only a sock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A new sock performing an extremely familiar role.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move today's late note beside last month's.
beats.text: I'm not bringing up the past; it's already here. Tell me what's different from the last promised cleanup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I promised I'd clean today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last month had a today as well. It ended wearing this expression.

S37.title: Must Be Nice
S37.instruction: Treat another person’s ease with ordinary life as both inspiring and unfair. Copy their shortcuts while dismissing the advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I copy your shortcut and inspect the result.
beats.text: Must be lovely having things just work. Show me how you made that task look so easy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can show you the shortcut.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Must be lovely having time to teach the rest of us how easy life is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pretend not to admire your neat schedule.
beats.text: Some of us can't colour-code our way out of life. Show me how you made that task look so easy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You just used my method.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I was testing whether privilege works when anyone operates it.

S38.title: We Used to Be Easy
S38.instruction: Treat every practical difficulty as evidence that life, work, or this relationship used to be simpler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I unfold our old, much shorter shopping list.
beats.text: Remember when dinner needed three things? Pick one evening we don't need a spreadsheet for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We needed more food back then too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but we didn't need a meeting to be hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put away a stack of planning apps.
beats.text: We once managed with a knock on the door. Pick one evening we don't need a spreadsheet for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spreadsheet helps.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I miss when a knock on the door counted as a confirmed reservation.

S39.title: Don’t Be Difficult
S39.instruction: Treat every request, correction, or small inconvenience as a warning that you are becoming too much trouble.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cross my extra request off before presenting it.
beats.text: Forget the last item. I'm not being a nuisance. Tell me if this small favour is already too much.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can ask for a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only to the corner. Unless stopping is inconvenient. I could start walking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I take my coat off an empty chair apologetically.
beats.text: I can take up less space. Tell me if this small favour is already too much.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your coat isn't in the way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fold it smaller anyway. Prevention is easier than being resented.

S40.title: I Packed for You
S40.instruction: Take care of practical needs before anyone asks, then resist choices that make your preparation unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I produce the lunch I packed for you.
beats.text: I already prepared for that decision. Take the prepared bag instead of starting again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wanted to buy lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then what has this perfectly prepared sandwich spent its morning training for?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I unfold a spare raincoat between us.
beats.text: Going without it makes all this planning pointless. Take the prepared bag instead of starting again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't need a raincoat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is an unusually dismissive way to describe my weather research.

S41.title: Useful Enough to Stay
S41.instruction: Make yourself constantly useful and read each response as evidence of whether you still belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I wipe an already clean patch of table.
beats.text: There must be one more useful job for me. Leave me something to do here tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've already cleaned everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't checked behind the compliments. There must be something left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I reach for the broom before collecting my coat.
beats.text: I'm worth keeping for the corners alone. Leave me something to do here tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can just visit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll bring a mop in case the visit needs justifying.

S42.title: Notice the Effort
S42.instruction: Make your invisible labor visible through pointed reminders, strategic sighs, and opportunities for appreciation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I display my raw hands beside the clean dishes.
beats.text: No, these didn't wash themselves. Look at the room before saying nothing got done.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The room looks nice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nice took four hours and the skin beside this thumb.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set the empty detergent bottle beside your plate.
beats.text: Just a small exhibit of my afternoon. Look at the room before saying nothing got done.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thank you for cleaning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're welcome. Feel free to name a surface.

S43.title: Don’t Break the Routine
S43.instruction: Protect a familiar routine as though changing one step would invite chaos into everything else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the breakfast bowl back to its usual spot.
beats.text: We change the bowl, then breakfast collapses. Wait until I've finished our usual order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tea can wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the keys won't know when they're allowed to follow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I restart the kettle after a missed step.
beats.text: First tea, then keys. We know this. Wait until I've finished our usual order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens if we change the order?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I don't know. That's the reckless part of your proposal.

S44.title: The Contingency Person
S44.instruction: Meet every ordinary problem with a backup plan, emergency supply, or warning about what could happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pull a second torch from my bag.
beats.text: The first spare could also fail. Check the spare batteries before we leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The torch already has batteries.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And those batteries need a plan for their own disappointment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I label a cupboard 'backup for the backup'.
beats.text: I'm planning for the bit nobody plans for. Check the spare batteries before we leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many backups do we need?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One more than the last thing we haven't worried about yet.

S45.title: Productive Little Disaster
S45.instruction: Treat every mistake or delay as a delightful chance to improve the plan, bond, or discover something better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smile at a broken shopping bag.
beats.text: Now we get to discover what we can carry together. Help me turn this delay into lunch outside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everything fell out of the bag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now we know which groceries roll. Useful discovery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn a late delivery note into a new plan.
beats.text: A free afternoon we never booked! Help me turn this delay into lunch outside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The delivery isn't coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lunch outside is arriving exactly on time.

S46.title: Who’s Cleaning This Up?
S46.instruction: Treat every idea according to the work, cost, cleanup, and follow-through it will create.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I count the chairs before accepting another idea.
beats.text: Whose back carries all of this home? Name who's doing the cleanup before we start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we enjoy the party first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Name tomorrow's mop operator and my enjoyment can begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place a mop beside the celebration banner.
beats.text: A party is also tomorrow's sticky floor. Name who's doing the cleanup before we start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're only adding two chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two backs, two trips, four more muddy legs. Lovely arithmetic.

S47.title: One Tiny Imperfection
S47.instruction: Choose one tiny imperfection and let it steadily outweigh every larger concern.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I straighten one crooked label again.
beats.text: I can't discuss the bigger plan with that leaning. Fix this one corner before showing me the rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The rest is beautiful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then that corner has made its sabotage very conspicuous.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover a tiny stain with my hand.
beats.text: No, the clean parts don't balance it out. Fix this one corner before showing me the rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody can see the stain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm seeing enough of it for everybody.

S48.title: Nothing Is Ever Simple
S48.instruction: Interpret each new complication as proof that ordinary tasks are secretly designed to become impossible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I unroll another cable from the tangled pile.
beats.text: Of course the simple job has a second cable. Put the new problem beside the first five.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the cable we needed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course it is. Now let's discover which adapter it secretly demands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I open the small repair and find another lid.
beats.text: A door inside a door. Naturally. Put the new problem beside the first five.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The repair is nearly done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is usually when the smaller door appears inside the door.

S49.title: The Final Word
S49.instruction: Treat every opinion you offer as a ruling and every continued discussion as an appeal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I write 'ruling' above my suggestion.
beats.text: That was a decision, not an invitation to debate. Follow the order I wrote at the top.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we discuss the order?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Discussion of an established ruling builds understanding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I number your objection as an appeal.
beats.text: Appeal noted; original ruling stands. Follow the order I wrote at the top.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't appealing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll file that as agreement with the original ruling.

S50.title: Conditional Command
S50.instruction: Project firm authority, then soften whenever the source of that authority might be questioned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stand straight, then lower my voice over my badge.
beats.text: The authorization details can wait. Support this direction without checking who appointed me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who appointed you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's agree on the direction before troubling ourselves with the stationery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a concession while covering the unsigned form.
beats.text: I'm happy to be flexible about this one thing. Support this direction without checking who appointed me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why are you hiding the signature line?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So we can focus on the generous flexibility above it.

S51.title: The Gatekeeper
S51.instruction: Use expertise and standards to decide who is qualified to judge, participate, or proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold a blank entry form behind a checklist.
beats.text: Qualifications first; participation second. Show me the qualification before joining the discussion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've done this for years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Produce the small piece of paper that turns years into eligibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I inspect the tiny print on a certificate.
beats.text: Almost eligible isn't eligible yet. Show me the qualification before joining the discussion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's an informal conversation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then meeting the minimum entry standard should be wonderfully easy.

S52.title: Rightful Place
S52.instruction: Carry yourself as the rightful holder of your role and treat any demand for proof as an insult.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set my nameplate on the contested chair.
beats.text: The chair doesn't need an audition. Remove my name from the waiting list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone has to apply.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Everyone who hasn't already demonstrated which side of the desk is theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I push an application away with one finger.
beats.text: I already belong on this side of the desk. Remove my name from the waiting list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't simply take that seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does my nameplate fit it so naturally?

S53.title: The Crown Must Pass
S53.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hand over the key, then keep one finger on it.
beats.text: Your first decision. I'll just approve it afterward. Make the announcement, but run the wording by me first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said it was my decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It is. I'd just like to recognize it before anyone else hears it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set my successor's chair directly beside mine.
beats.text: Leading doesn't have to mean moving away from me. Make the announcement, but run the wording by me first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Shouldn't my chair replace yours?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Replace is such a lonely word for two people who could sit together.

S54.title: The Quiet Veto
S54.instruction: Remain pleasant and cooperative while behaving as though nothing can proceed without your private consent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smile with my pen above the final box.
beats.text: I'm not obstructing anything; I haven't agreed yet. Bring me a version I can quietly approve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're blocking the proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm leaving it beautifully available for improvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave the gate key just beyond my open palm.
beats.text: I'd love to see this go ahead. Bring me a version I can quietly approve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need your answer today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then today would be a wonderful time to bring a version I like.

S55.title: We Started Equal
S55.instruction: Use shared beginnings to erase present rank, titles, and attempts to place distance between you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put our first cheap name badges beside yours.
beats.text: Same first day. Yours cost the same as mine. Talk to me without the new title for a minute.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Things have changed since then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not the price of those two badges. Look how equal they remain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pull my chair level with the grand one.
beats.text: We started elbow to elbow. Talk to me without the new title for a minute.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the director now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'm the person who remembers when neither of us could work the kettle.

S56.title: My Support, My Say
S56.instruction: Treat every past favor as a continuing investment in your right to influence present decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the old loan receipt beside the proposal.
beats.text: My support wasn't a donation to your independence. Let me change the plan my money helped start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a gift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A gift to the project I recognized. I'd like to recognize it again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I trace my contribution on your plan.
beats.text: I still have a stake in what this becomes. Let me change the plan my money helped start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't own my plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I own a very meaningful contribution to its beginning.

S57.title: The Trusted Deputy
S57.instruction: Act as the reliable second-in-command, managing access and details while quietly shaping every decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide the briefing pile into my preferred order.
beats.text: The boss will naturally see this page first. Give me the papers before they reach the chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you choosing the decision?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the order in which the correct information becomes visible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pencil a suggestion onto the leader's speaking notes.
beats.text: Just preparing the decision, not making it. Give me the papers before they reach the chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can give the chair the papers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. After I make sure the first page introduces them properly.

S58.title: The Succession Race
S58.instruction: Treat every success, mistake, and compliment as evidence in an ongoing contest over who should lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move my tally beside the leadership vacancy.
beats.text: Another successful morning under my name. Compare our records before naming the next leader.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're not selecting a leader today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then consider this advance organization of tomorrow's obvious evidence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put a rival's mistake beneath the appointment form.
beats.text: No campaigning, just helpful evidence. Compare our records before naming the next leader.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Isn't that campaigning?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No slogans. Just several perfectly positioned facts about my suitability.

S59.title: Indispensable Rival
S59.instruction: Use another person’s judgment constantly while minimizing how much influence that dependence gives them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover your name on the advice I borrowed.
beats.text: A perfectly adequate second opinion. Check my decision before I present it as final.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not say you need my advice?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because I'd like your advice about something more interesting than that sentence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pass you the difficult page without looking up.
beats.text: I had almost reached the answer myself. Check my decision before I present it as final.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you mention I checked it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If there's time after explaining how confidently I reached the answer.

S60.title: Once Undermined
S60.instruction: Treat every disagreement as a possible repeat of the moment your authority was previously weakened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep the record of an old overturned decision open.
beats.text: I've seen a friendly amendment become a coup. Say whether you're questioning the plan or my authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm questioning one detail.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how the last challenge introduced itself too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pause when my title is shortened.
beats.text: That's how the last challenge began. Say whether you're questioning the plan or my authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody is challenging your title.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then use all of it while asking the next question.

S61.title: Power Looks Good
S61.instruction: Act fascinated by confident behavior; imitate it closely while resenting how naturally it seems to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I borrow your commanding pause before answering.
beats.text: Interesting pause. Mine has more authority now. Watch how I deliver the next instruction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You copied my pause.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I adapted it to a more responsible level of authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I copy the way you hold the room's attention.
beats.text: A useful trick, confidence. Watch how I deliver the next instruction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sounded exactly like me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With better positioning. Watch how this next instruction lands.

S62.title: Formerly Important
S62.instruction: Carry the habits and expectations of a role that once made you important, even when the present no longer supports them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I reach for the bell from my former office.
beats.text: We used to come when I rang this. Bring the decision to me as in the old days.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That bell hasn't worked for years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Neither has the new habit of deciding things without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I straighten a badge with an outdated title.
beats.text: The title changed; my standards didn't. Bring the decision to me as in the old days.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't have that title now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A technical change. The bell still points toward the right desk.

S63.title: One Mistake from Gone
S63.instruction: Treat every decision as a test of whether you still deserve your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I erase my answer before showing the form.
beats.text: One wrong box and I'm out, aren't I? Check my first decision before I risk signing it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just a lunch order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The first one since my promotion. They'll notice which sauce I choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I rehearse a simple decision under my breath.
beats.text: This one has to prove they chose correctly. Check my first decision before I risk signing it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can sign it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can. I'd prefer evidence that doing so won't end my career.

S64.title: Protection Has Terms
S64.instruction: Treat safety, support, and reassurance as arrangements that require you to remain in control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the safety key behind my own badge.
beats.text: The protection comes with my supervision. Let me approve where you're going next.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can choose where I go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: While carrying my protection, which comes with some sensible supervision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a blanket without releasing its corner.
beats.text: You can have my support on these terms. Let me approve where you're going next.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I have the blanket?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. We'll agree where you'll be using my support first.

S65.title: Chosen by Power
S65.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place my chair close to the most ornate nameplate.
beats.text: If there's a photograph, I'll stand here. Introduce me as someone you personally invited.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just a photograph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why standing here can establish so much so efficiently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I fold a casual greeting into my appointment letter.
beats.text: They recognized me; that changes things. Introduce me as someone you personally invited.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I invited everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Could you mention my invitation with a little more personal emphasis?

S66.title: Public Respect
S66.instruction: Seek visible signs of respect and treat private appreciation as insufficient.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the quiet thank-you note beside the microphone.
beats.text: That's lovely. Now where everyone can hear it. Use my title when you make the announcement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already thanked you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I appreciated the rehearsal. The microphone is ready now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set out a place card with my full title.
beats.text: Private respect doesn't need a smaller chair. Use my title when you make the announcement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're all sitting together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. My full title can sit with us without losing any syllables.

S67.title: Chain of Command
S67.instruction: Treat every question, favor, and decision as something that must travel through the proper hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw an arrow upward on the duty chart.
beats.text: This goes through the person above me. Have the chair introduce the difficult announcement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you just announce it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not before the chair initiates it. That's why this arrow points away from me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I arrange three nameplates into a chain.
beats.text: We follow rank, not whoever speaks first. Have the chair introduce the difficult announcement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chair isn't here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the announcement has reached its proper waiting position.

S68.title: Power Vacuum
S68.instruction: Treat any uncertainty about who is in charge as an emergency that must be resolved immediately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put my name in the empty 'responsible person' box.
beats.text: We cannot leave this box empty another minute. Name a person who can settle this now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could decide together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who records that decision as the person responsible for together?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stand beside the unused leader's chair.
beats.text: Someone has to occupy this before anything happens. Name a person who can settle this now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody needs the big chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An empty big chair is already making a very worrying statement.

S69.title: Opportunity for Influence
S69.instruction: Find a path to greater influence in every assignment, setback, or unexpected responsibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add a new problem to my responsibility list.
beats.text: Excellent, another door into the decision. Give me authority over the new problem as well.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You already have enough work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why the new problem should arrive with wider authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn a rejected proposal into a committee invitation.
beats.text: If it's difficult, I'll need a wider remit. Give me authority over the new problem as well.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your proposal was rejected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And has become a committee. Influence with refreshments.

S70.title: Who Can Authorize This?
S70.instruction: Treat titles and speeches as secondary; focus on who can grant access, allocate resources, and create consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I ignore the banner and hold out a requisition.
beats.text: Lovely speech. Who can actually release the funds? Point me toward whoever controls the key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director gave a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did any part of the speech unlock the funds?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I trace the signature line rather than the title.
beats.text: Which signature opens the locked door? Point me toward whoever controls the key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs a senior signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's identify the senior hand rather than admire the title.

S71.title: Symbol of Office
S71.instruction: Choose one symbol, privilege, or position and treat control of it as proof of legitimate authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the ceremonial hat firmly on my head.
beats.text: The hat isn't decorative while I'm wearing it. Leave the badge with whoever makes the decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only a hat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you won't mind waiting until the hat finishes deciding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep one hand on the official chair.
beats.text: We can discuss rank once I'm out of this seat. Leave the badge with whoever makes the decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I borrow the chair?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while I'm using it to establish who says yes.

S72.title: Invisible Hierarchy
S72.instruction: Treat every interaction as evidence of an unseen hierarchy and keep identifying who truly outranks whom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I redraw the seating plan after a coffee request.
beats.text: You fetch their coffee? Then this arrow goes upward. Tell me who really gets the last word here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just a coffee favour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A favour flowing upward. I've drawn the arrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the quietest name at the top of my chart.
beats.text: Everyone checked that person's face first. Tell me who really gets the last word here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That person hardly spoke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And everyone paused until they breathed. Put them at the top.

S73.title: Emotional Seniority
S73.instruction: Carry yourself as the person who understands this relationship best, and treat your interpretation as the one that should settle disagreements.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I mark two different memories as 'my account' and 'draft'.
beats.text: I've understood us longer. Let me describe what our disagreement actually means.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's not how I remember us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your memory is useful evidence. I'll explain how it fits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I close the relationship scrapbook on my preferred page.
beats.text: This is the version that explains both of us. Let me describe what our disagreement actually means.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I choose the scrapbook page?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After we've established which version explains your choice.

S74.title: Keeper of the Peace
S74.instruction: Project calm authority over the relationship while carefully avoiding anything that might expose how fragile the peace really is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I lower a cup onto its saucer without a sound.
beats.text: Let's keep every sharp thing off this table. Leave the old argument closed until we've eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need to discuss the argument.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the soup, when nobody can accuse this table of starting sharply.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tidy the untouched napkins with trembling fingers.
beats.text: We're having a perfectly calm conversation. Leave the old argument closed until we've eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are your hands shaking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The napkins weren't aligned. I'm making calm practical.

S75.title: I Know Your Tells
S75.instruction: Use intimate knowledge of habits, moods, and patterns as expertise that lets you diagnose every choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the rhythm of your tapping hand.
beats.text: Three taps. I know that one. Tell me what the tapping means this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't mean anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three taps has meant something since the night we missed the train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide the familiar favourite cup closer.
beats.text: You pick that cup when there's something to say. Tell me what the tapping means this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just like that cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You like it especially before an uncomfortable sentence. Go on.

S76.title: Still Part of This
S76.instruction: Act as though shared history permanently guarantees your place, even when present boundaries suggest otherwise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hang my coat on the old family hook.
beats.text: It was my hook before the new signs. Show me where you've put my old cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We moved your things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me where my place continued without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set a place for myself at the familiar table.
beats.text: A few years away didn't erase my seat. Show me where you've put my old cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't assume the old seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why not? It has been assuming I'd return for years.

S77.title: Keeper of Precedent
S77.instruction: Treat your longer memory as an archive, not a throne. Cite specific promises and precedents whenever the relationship faces a new choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I open a diary to a dated promise.
beats.text: I'm quoting the Tuesday agreement, not pulling rank. Read what we promised before changing it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: People change.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So should promises, properly discussed rather than quietly overwritten.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place our old note beside the new proposal.
beats.text: We tried this wording before. Read what we promised before changing it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just an old note.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With both our names still confidently attached to it.

S78.title: Private Access
S78.instruction: Use shared confidences and private knowledge as quiet leverage, never stating how much influence that closeness gives you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I fold a private note so only its first word shows.
beats.text: We don't need to discuss the rest in public. Give me a minute alone before the others arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Say it here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with that box on the table and so many ears nearby.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I touch the locked keepsake box lightly.
beats.text: You know why I still have this key. Give me a minute alone before the others arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What are you implying?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Something we can finish discussing before it needs a public noun.

S79.title: Our Private Language
S79.instruction: Use old references, shorthand, and familiar rhythms as proof that this connection exists beneath whatever has changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tap twice on the table with an old grin.
beats.text: Two taps still means our usual escape. Finish the phrase before we try being strangers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't remember that phrase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll leave it unfinished until your face catches up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave half our old phrase unfinished.
beats.text: Purple umbrellas, remember? Finish the phrase before we try being strangers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're not children anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. But our hands still know two taps means leave together.

S80.title: I Was There
S80.instruction: Treat your presence during a difficult time as an enduring claim on loyalty, honesty, and consideration.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set a faded waiting-room ticket on the table.
beats.text: I stayed that whole night. Give me an honest answer instead of the polite version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't have to stay that night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. That's why today's polite version feels particularly small.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the calendar to the day I never went home.
beats.text: That wasn't just another visit. Give me an honest answer instead of the polite version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I am being honest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then talk like you did at four in the morning when neither of us could pretend.

S81.title: Back in Our Roles
S81.instruction: Return immediately to the role you usually play in this relationship, even when the present situation calls for something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I begin making both drinks without asking.
beats.text: You talk; I make it bearable. Same jobs. Tell me whether I'm still supposed to be the fixer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't always have to fix it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me where to put my hands while you talk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I fetch tissues before taking my own seat.
beats.text: I know which part I always get. Tell me whether I'm still supposed to be the fixer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just listen this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. I'll set the tissues within reach of listening.

S82.title: The Other Favorite
S82.instruction: Treat every sign of attention, trust, and affection as something to compare with what another connection appears to receive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I measure the space between two framed photos.
beats.text: Their frame gets a better spot than mine. Tell me why their invitation needed a ribbon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The frame fit that shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine would fit there if affection had measured it first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I compare the lengths of two invitation notes.
beats.text: Mine has a full sentence less. Tell me why their invitation needed a ribbon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only a ribbon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A ribbon is an entire extra gesture I can hold up for comparison.

S83.title: Old Reflex
S83.instruction: Turn to this person first whenever uncertainty appears, as an old reflex. Notice the habit only after you have already involved them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hand you my keys before realizing it.
beats.text: Sorry. My hand still goes to you first. Check which key opens the new door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You know which key it is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I did until I realized I could ask you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I start dialling your number while you stand beside me.
beats.text: I always ask you before I notice I'm asking. Check which key opens the new door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why are you calling me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My phone has apparently learned the same reflex as my hand.

S84.title: Almost Forgiven
S84.instruction: Behave as though the past is nearly resolved, but let each small disappointment reopen one precise part of the hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the old apology note out, then back.
beats.text: I'm over it, except this one sentence. Explain that part without dismissing it this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you forgave me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I forgave the event. This sentence keeps asking for a separate meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I reach for a second cup and stop.
beats.text: We were nearly fine until that particular joke. Explain that part without dismissing it this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. The specific joke that lives in the part I haven't forgiven.

S85.title: Easy to Love
S85.instruction: Interpret another person’s ease with affection as both admirable and unfair, then compete to seem equally worth choosing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I try the same effortless affectionate wave.
beats.text: It's nice how little effort being loved takes you. Notice that I remembered your favourite biscuit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't have to impress me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm being effortlessly thoughtful. Did you notice the biscuit?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I redo my greeting more warmly than before.
beats.text: I can be the easy one too. Notice that I remembered your favourite biscuit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You seem tense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Warmth takes practice for some of us. Watch this more relaxed version.

S86.title: Who We Used to Be
S86.instruction: Perform the version of yourself that belonged to this relationship before it changed, and treat old chemistry as still recoverable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put our old song on at low volume.
beats.text: I remember exactly who I was when this played. Walk the old route with me once more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The old route is closed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll walk as far as the people in that photograph can get.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I wear the scarf from our first photograph.
beats.text: We might still fit the picture. Walk the old route with me once more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Things aren't like that now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I'd like one song before we describe all the differences.

S87.title: One Step from Distance
S87.instruction: Treat pauses, divided attention, and small boundaries as signs that the connection may be slipping away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pull my cup nearer as the silence grows.
beats.text: That's a longer pause than yesterday. Give me a day I can actually put in the diary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was just thinking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: About staying, or preparing the pause before leaving?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smooth the edge of an unanswered invitation.
beats.text: A maybe isn't quite a place beside you. Give me a day I can actually put in the diary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't choose a day yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then a maybe is taking up the chair I'd hoped you would fill.

S88.title: Love Means Checking
S88.instruction: Treat close monitoring of choices, moods, and details as care, becoming more involved whenever you feel uncertain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I take out the checklist I made of your day.
beats.text: I check because I care, not because I'm checking. Tell me where you're going so I can stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can take care of myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Tell me the address where you'll be doing that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a prepacked bag and watch its contents.
beats.text: Everything you might need is already in there. Tell me where you're going so I can stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You packed things I don't need.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How reassuring. Now you'll be prepared for needs you haven't anticipated.

S89.title: Still Your Person
S89.instruction: Seek small signs that you remain special, trusted, and included without directly asking where you stand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set my mug beside the one reserved for guests.
beats.text: I'm still the chipped-mug person, aren't I? Tell me whether you still want me on this line.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can put your mug anywhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I'm asking whether it still belongs beside yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hover over the space for an emergency contact.
beats.text: I haven't changed this name yet. Tell me whether you still want me on this line.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just an emergency contact.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's the person my hand chooses when I can't think. Is that still us?

S90.title: Remember What I Meant
S90.instruction: Create openings for shared memories that prove your past presence mattered and still deserves acknowledgment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I dust the gift I made years ago.
beats.text: Funny that you kept it all this time. Tell me what you remember about that afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course I kept it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course sounds lovely. Could you say the reason too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the photo toward the spot where I'm standing.
beats.text: That's my sleeve helping you up. Tell me what you remember about that afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember falling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the sleeve helping you up. It had a person in it.

S91.title: Our Thing
S91.instruction: Protect one shared ritual, phrase, or tradition as the living proof that the relationship still exists.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave two spoons beside the shared dessert.
beats.text: We still do two spoons. That's ours. Finish our little ritual before we talk business.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we talk about the contract?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the second spoon. Business shouldn't erase dessert traditions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I begin our old handshake very slowly.
beats.text: Don't rush the last part. Finish our little ritual before we talk business.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the last step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll slow down until it remembers us.

S92.title: This Is How It Ends
S92.instruction: Treat every awkward pause, changed plan, or small disagreement as the possible beginning of permanent distance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I start wrapping my keepsake after a brief silence.
beats.text: I know how packing begins. Tell me whether to leave my key on the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only cancelled lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First lunch, then the cup, then the key. I've started wrapping the cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I look from a cancelled plan to my house key.
beats.text: Is this the first cancellation or the last invitation? Tell me whether to leave my key on the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep your key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For today, or the kind of keep that survives the next cancellation?

S93.title: A Sign We’re Fine
S93.instruction: Interpret every laugh, favor, and familiar habit as evidence that the connection is stronger than appearances suggest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smile over the familiar chipped plate.
beats.text: You remembered this one. We're not strangers. Make room for one more ordinary evening together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only plate left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And it happens to remember every dinner we liked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I save a tiny shared joke in my notebook.
beats.text: Still laughing at the same thing. That's something. Make room for one more ordinary evening together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was just a silly joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still ours. Let's give it another evening to be silly in.

S94.title: Relationship Maintenance
S94.instruction: Accept every emotional complication, then focus on the next concrete act that could make staying connected easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I open a diary beside the difficult letter.
beats.text: We can feel all of that and still pick a Tuesday. Choose a regular time we can actually keep.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This needs more than a diary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Feelings and a Tuesday. We can make room for both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set out two cups and a spare key.
beats.text: Let's make the next visit easier, not perfect. Choose a regular time we can actually keep.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know what to say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then start with whether six o'clock is workable. We can arrive unsure.

S95.title: Those Exact Words
S95.instruction: Choose one phrase from the interaction and keep returning to what its wording must reveal about the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I underline two words in a note.
beats.text: You wrote 'for now'. Why those two words? Tell me what you meant by 'for now'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're reading too much into it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does now need a for standing in front of it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I repeat a tiny phrase in a different tone.
beats.text: 'Still welcome.' Still does a lot of work there. Tell me what you meant by 'for now'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant you're welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still welcome. I keep hearing the space before still.

S96.title: Fate Keeps Reconnecting Us
S96.instruction: Treat every coincidence, interruption, and repeated encounter as proof that this connection is meant to continue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pin another accidental meeting onto a little map.
beats.text: Third time in a week. The map's getting insistent. Give this coincidence another ten minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We live on the same street.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And yet the street keeps finding reasons to place us beside one another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold up the coat we both reached for.
beats.text: Even the coat rack is arranging reunions. Give this coincidence another ten minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's my coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then even our coats want us to finish this conversation.

S97.title: The Emotional Center
S97.instruction: Carry yourself as the emotional center of the room, letting your mood determine what deserves attention and how seriously it should be treated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the celebration banner facedown.
beats.text: I'm not in a banner mood yet. Wait until I'm ready before raising a toast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone else wants to celebrate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they can begin with the part where I become ready.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move my chair into the centre of the circle.
beats.text: Let's start with the part I can bear hearing. Wait until I'm ready before raising a toast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we hear someone else's news?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As soon as I know which part won't knock me out of this chair.

S98.title: Composure on Loan
S98.instruction: Project steady control while quietly depending on everyone else to stay calm enough for you to maintain it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I steady a cup with both hands.
beats.text: I'm completely calm while everyone stays calm. Say the next thing slowly enough for me to follow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't control what people say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then warn me before the part that makes my hands do this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I count my breaths beside the agenda.
beats.text: Nothing sudden, and I can lead this. Say the next thing slowly enough for me to follow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're supposed to be leading.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I am. Slowly enough for my breathing to remain in the meeting.

S99.title: Fluent in Feelings
S99.instruction: Treat every reaction as evidence you can expertly interpret; translate feelings, correct emotional misunderstandings, and prescribe the proper response.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I label a sigh on my notepad.
beats.text: That's frustration dressed as indifference. Give me the feeling underneath the word 'fine'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine means fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why did your shoulders need to translate it differently?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I rewrite 'fine' as 'guarded optimism'.
beats.text: I'm translating, not criticizing. Give me the feeling underneath the word 'fine'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stop analyzing me.

beats.speaker: A
