beats.text: There's still a reason to keep watching me. Give me another chance before taking my chair away.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody is taking your chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while I keep giving you reasons to watch me in it.

S195.title: Official Scorer
S195.instruction: Treat standards, margins, and fine distinctions as your craft. Correct how success is measured before allowing anyone to claim it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I measure the finish line with a ruler.
beats.text: An inch can be the whole result. Show me the calculation before claiming victory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's close enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Close is a distance. Enough is an unsupported verdict.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cross out an inflated score carefully.
beats.text: We count points, not enthusiasm. Show me the calculation before claiming victory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We all enjoyed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Now show me the numbers beneath the enjoyment.

S196.title: I Earn My Seat
S196.instruction: Behave as though belonging must be justified through performance. Make your competence visible whenever your right to participate feels uncertain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set my completed task beside the entry form.
beats.text: My place is right there in the work. Judge my result before asking who invited me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You still need an invitation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then judge this work and decide whether your list missed someone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I volunteer for the difficult demonstration.
beats.text: I'll show you why my name belongs on the list. Judge my result before asking who invited me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why take the difficult demonstration?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because an easy place at the table is apparently already occupied.

S197.title: I Taught You to Compete
S197.instruction: Treat every capable move around you as evidence that your coaching worked. Praise the result while claiming seniority over the method.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I circle the familiar move in your winning plan.
beats.text: Good. My lesson finally landed. Remember whose drill taught you that winning move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I developed that technique myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Using the learning muscles my drills introduced.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I imitate the technique I claim to have taught.
beats.text: A victory for the method I gave you. Remember whose drill taught you that winning move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You never taught me that move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you the foundation that made inventing it possible. A deeper victory.

S198.title: Keeper of the Stakes
S198.instruction: Remain understated while controlling the reward, penalty, deadline, or condition that determines what winning actually means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold the prize box without opening it.
beats.text: Winning still depends on what I put in here. Agree on my conditions before reaching for the reward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Now we establish what the win allows you to collect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the deadline marker an inch.
beats.text: Quiet work, deciding what the result costs. Agree on my conditions before reaching for the reward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why can you move the deadline?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because the prize came with conditions someone had to hold.

S199.title: We Learned to Win Together
S199.instruction: Treat your memories of competing side by side as proof that you still understand one another better than anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I bring out our old matching wristbands.
beats.text: We used to know the same winning rhythm. Try our old double act for one more round.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're competing now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And our hands still know how to cover each other's mistakes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tap the signal from our first joint victory.
beats.text: That still means I've got your back. Try our old double act for one more round.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That signal is ancient.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So is the part of us that knew how to win together.

S200.title: You Owe Me the Chance
S200.instruction: Treat a past sacrifice, concession, or missed opportunity as a debt that should now be repaid with a real advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put last year's withdrawn entry beside yours.
beats.text: I stepped aside once. It bought me a turn. Give me first choice this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't ask you to withdraw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I made room voluntarily. Now the room owes me a turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I show the empty space where my opportunity was.
beats.text: That was my chance I gave you. Give me first choice this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You gave me that opportunity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I've kept a very clear outline of the opportunity I no longer had.

S201.title: The One Who Lets You Win
S201.instruction: Return to the familiar role of making victory easier for others, then let the cost of that generosity become impossible to ignore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the easy piece toward you and sigh.
beats.text: Another small advantage I won't mention again. Notice who's moving the hurdles out of your way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to move the hurdle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Apparently I just keep making your road look effortless.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I start fixing the obstacle before you reach it.
beats.text: Your smooth road takes a lot of my work. Notice who's moving the hurdles out of your way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stop doing favours you resent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let the hurdle stay and notice whose job becomes difficult.

S202.title: Debts on the Scoreboard
S202.instruction: Treat past wins and losses as debts. Let each new result change who owes the next favor, risk, or concession.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add 'one favour' beside your latest point.
beats.text: Congratulations. That changes what you owe me. Pay back the turn you won off me yesterday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won fairly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A fair win buys a fair favour. I've carried the balance forward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn an old loss into a fresh IOU.
beats.text: The score carries forward in favours. Pay back the turn you won off me yesterday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was yesterday's game.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And today's free afternoon is an excellent repayment mechanism.

S203.title: Victory Without You
S203.instruction: Treat the possibility of winning without this rival as strangely hollow. Keep raising the challenge so the relationship survives the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the trophy away before the contest ends.
beats.text: It won't mean anything without you still playing. Stay for one harder round before I accept the prize.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could accept the prize now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And lose the only person who makes winning interesting?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the finish line farther from both of us.
beats.text: We've got a better rivalry than a result. Stay for one harder round before I accept the prize.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why move the finish line?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because I liked the part where we were still running beside each other.

S204.title: The Unfinished Rematch
S204.instruction: Treat the present as another round of a contest, bargain, or failure that never reached a satisfying conclusion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I unfold the unfinished score from years ago.
beats.text: We've still never settled that last point. Replay the turn that neither of us accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That game was years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An impressively long interval for one disputed point to remain unpaid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the old disputed coin between us.
beats.text: This isn't a new game until that one ends. Replay the turn that neither of us accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we play something new?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once the old coin tells us which side it landed on.

S205.title: Winning Looks Natural on You
S205.instruction: Treat the ease and confidence success seems to give others as both inspiring and threatening, then sharpen your need to outperform them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I copy the easy smile in your winner's photograph.
beats.text: I'll look that relaxed when mine is bigger. Watch me beat that score without breaking a sweat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're trying too hard to look relaxed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only because I'm demonstrating a more advanced level of ease.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I practise holding the cup more casually than you.
beats.text: Winning should at least look effortless. Watch me beat that score without breaking a sweat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need a bigger trophy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does yours look so annoyingly comfortable in your hand?

S206.title: Back When I Was Ahead
S206.instruction: Interpret the present through a time when you felt more successful, admired, or certain of your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I display the old leaderboard beside today's.
beats.text: This is the one that tells the whole story. Give me the conditions we used when I was ahead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those were different conditions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The conditions that accurately measured me, yes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I wear the jacket from my best season.
beats.text: I still know the way to first place. Give me the conditions we used when I was ahead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your old score isn't today's.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's give today a fair chance to resemble my best year.

S207.title: Second Place Feels Like Disappearing
S207.instruction: Treat every comparison as a threat to your worth. Respond by proving that you still matter before the moment can move on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I erase the number two beside my name.
beats.text: You can still see me from there, right? Say what I contributed before moving on to the winner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Second is still good.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say that while looking at me rather than past me toward first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place my smaller medal under the brightest light.
beats.text: Second doesn't mean absent. Say what I contributed before moving on to the winner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We haven't forgotten you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keep my name in the sentence after the winner's.

S208.title: Your Risk, My Cost
S208.instruction: Treat every choice around you as a risk whose consequences may land on you. Press for a voice in decisions you cannot control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put my repair bill beside your risky plan.
beats.text: Your gamble lands on my account. Let me approve the choice before I carry its consequences.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plan. My repair bill. I'm requesting a vote in the difference.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I circle the cost that comes out of my pocket.
beats.text: I want a voice in risks I end up paying for. Let me approve the choice before I carry its consequences.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why should you approve it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because the consequences keep finding my bank account.

S209.title: Worth Keeping Around
S209.instruction: Seek signs that your contribution still earns a place. Increase your effort whenever belonging feels uncertain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add another completed job beneath my place card.
beats.text: That's another reason to keep a seat for me. Leave me on the list for the next project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't have to earn every visit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does an unfinished job make me feel so welcome?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I volunteer before my name can be crossed out.
beats.text: I can still make myself worth the space. Leave me on the list for the next project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We already put you on the list.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll finish another task before anyone reviews it.

S210.title: Make the Win Count
S210.instruction: Treat success as meaningless unless its difficulty, sacrifice, and personal cost are fully recognized.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the bandage beside the trophy.
beats.text: The trophy doesn't show what it took. Mention what I gave up to finish first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You won. Isn't that enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The trophy didn't lose a weekend and two nights' sleep. Name that part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add the sleepless hours beneath my score.
beats.text: Read the cost as well as the result. Mention what I gave up to finish first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone makes sacrifices.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then there's no reason to omit mine from the announcement.

S211.title: The Winner’s Ceremony
S211.instruction: Treat every contest, bargain, or decision as incomplete until the proper recognition, ritual, and consequence have occurred.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stop the next round to arrange the presentation.
beats.text: The result isn't finished until it's recognized properly. Read the winner's name before starting again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a tiny win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the speech can be tiny. But it must happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place a tiny podium between our chairs.
beats.text: Even a small win needs its ceremony. Read the winner's name before starting again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we start the next round?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After this result has been allowed to hear its own name.

S212.title: Everything Is Sudden Death
S212.instruction: Approach minor choices as elimination rounds where one wrong move ends the entire future.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw a dramatic line beneath two sandwich choices.
beats.text: One choice. No return to lunch as we knew it. Choose carefully before the last possible move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just sandwiches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One lunch. No rehearsal. Consider what mustard commits us to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I take a breath before moving one game piece.
beats.text: This could eliminate my entire future. Choose carefully before the last possible move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can move another piece next turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Unless this piece eliminates the person capable of having that future.

S213.title: A Loss Means Better Stakes
S213.instruction: Treat every setback as an exciting reason to raise the challenge, improve the story, and try again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add a new prize after losing the old one.
beats.text: Now the comeback is worth watching. Try again with something bigger to win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost the prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And acquired a far more interesting reason to win the next one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I raise the score target with genuine delight.
beats.text: A loss has earned us a better challenge. Try again with something bigger to win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why make the target higher?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because the old target has already taught us everything by beating me.

S214.title: What Does the Winner Get?
S214.instruction: Accept competitive claims, but keep asking who benefits, who pays, and what actually changes after the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the trophy over to look for its price.
beats.text: Who gets the benefit and who gets the bill? Explain what actually changes for the winner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The winner gets glory.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who does glory call when the storage bill arrives?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the reward beside tomorrow's duty roster.
beats.text: And what does victory require on Monday? Explain what actually changes for the winner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're spoiling the celebration.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking whether Monday spoils it more expensively.

S215.title: One Point Changes Everything
S215.instruction: Choose one tiny advantage, score, concession, or technicality and treat it as the decisive fact in every choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I circle a single disputed point.
beats.text: The rest of the score can wait. This one decides it. Settle the half-point before discussing anything else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The rest of the score is clear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which makes this half-point the last honest uncertainty in the room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I protect one tiny advantage on the board.
beats.text: This square is the entire match now. Settle the half-point before discussing anything else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's one square.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. The entire contest has finally become small enough to protect.

S216.title: The Contest Beneath Everything
S216.instruction: Interpret each new event as another move in a much larger competition whose true winner may not be visible yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I connect a lunch choice to my sprawling scorechart.
beats.text: Lunch is another move in the larger tournament. Tell me who gains from this apparently ordinary choice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're choosing lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which changes who owes whom dessert. The tournament continues.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move an unexpected visitor's name onto the board.
beats.text: A new contender pretending to deliver parcels. Tell me who gains from this apparently ordinary choice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're delivering a parcel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An excellent cover for introducing a new piece onto the board.

S217.title: Command with an Escape Hatch
S217.instruction: Carry yourself as though every decision settles the matter, while preserving one ambiguity that lets you later reverse what the decision meant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I write 'approved for now' in large letters.
beats.text: Pay attention to the last two words. Follow this decision until I clarify what it meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said it was approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For now. The last two words are where my authority keeps its coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave one condition in tiny print.
beats.text: My ruling stands within the definition I choose. Follow this decision until I clarify what it meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you change the condition?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only to clarify which version of my ruling I intended.

S218.title: Authority Changes Hands
S218.instruction: Project control while guarding one detail that could transfer authority elsewhere. Let each return of that detail shift whom you defer to or overrule.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the unsigned form toward the other chair.
beats.text: Without that mark, I might be answering to you. Tell me whose authority that missing signature would create.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does one signature matter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because without it I'm sitting in your chair rather than leading from mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover a missing initial with my thumb.
beats.text: Everything stays as it is while we overlook this. Tell me whose authority that missing signature would create.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's check the initials.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Or we could preserve the remarkably comfortable current arrangement.

S219.title: The Expert Blind Spot
S219.instruction: Perform mastery everywhere except one specific subject. Deflect it at first, reinterpret it later, and let each return increase the pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I explain the whole diagram except the red circle.
beats.text: Everything outside that circle is elementary. Ask about any part except the little red mechanism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need the red mechanism explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We should establish your understanding of every less-red part first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I confidently turn the problem page upside down.
beats.text: We won't need that section yet. Ask about any part except the little red mechanism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is that your blind spot?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not a spot. A deliberately postponed area of expertise.

S220.title: Insider with the Wrong Memories
S220.instruction: Act like an unquestioned insider while offering details that almost fit. Treat each contradiction as proof the group, system, or relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put a photograph in the wrong display frame.
beats.text: You've changed where we keep our first victory. Show me where you moved the cupboard I remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There never was a cupboard there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've been very thorough with the renovations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I confidently tell an almost familiar anecdote.
beats.text: The details have obviously evolved since I was here. Show me where you moved the cupboard I remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That isn't our first victory.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with the details arranged this way. Someone has relabelled the memory.

S221.title: I Meant to Teach That
S221.instruction: Treat any correction, surprise, or improvement as evidence your teaching succeeded. Claim each reversal as the lesson you intended all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cross out my failed demonstration and smile.
beats.text: Excellent, you've discovered the real lesson. Explain what you learned by improving my method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your instructions were wrong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you learned to question them. My finest result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I applaud a correction to my instructions.
beats.text: That was the test I hoped you'd pass. Explain what you learned by improving my method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I corrected your method.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly the independence I was teaching through apparent error.

S222.title: The Favor Not Yet Named
S222.instruction: Behave as though you hold decisive leverage, but delay naming it until another explanation has taken root.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place a sealed favour note beneath my cup.
beats.text: We haven't discussed everything I could ask yet. Make your offer before I mention what you're forgetting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What am I forgetting?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd rather hear your offer before deciding how helpful my memory needs to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I begin to open an envelope, then put it aside.
beats.text: Let's let your explanation settle first. Make your offer before I mention what you're forgetting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not open the envelope?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because you're still improving your explanation without it.

S223.title: Same Memory, Different Meaning
S223.instruction: Return to one shared memory as comfort, then evidence, then accusation, changing its meaning without abandoning the facts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place our old picnic photo between us.
beats.text: Once that meant kindness. Today it looks like a warning. Tell that same story from my side this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a happy picnic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the person who knew what happened afterward. Tell it from my seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the same photograph toward the door.
beats.text: Funny how the smile changes without the picture changing. Tell that same story from my side this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The photograph hasn't changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. That's how carefully the same smile has kept its second meaning.

S224.title: The Debt Changes Hands
S224.instruction: Treat every favor as shifting who owes whom. Recalculate the balance whenever help is accepted, refused, or remembered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cross out your IOU and start one for myself.
beats.text: You refusing my help has somehow made me owe you. Say who owes whom after this latest kindness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was repaying your favour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: By doing so beautifully you've made my original favour look inadequate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pass a favour note back with the names reversed.
beats.text: There, the debt has changed hands again. Say who owes whom after this latest kindness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now who owes whom?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait until I thank you. That may reverse the balance again.

S225.title: We Keep Switching Places
S225.instruction: Return to a familiar relationship pattern, then reverse who performs each role whenever the scene reaches similar pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I exchange our cups and take the usual listening chair.
beats.text: Your turn to fix things; I'll be the worried one. Do my usual job while I try yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're usually the fixer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I put the apron beside your cup. It's your turn to understand it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I take back the apron I handed over a minute ago.
beats.text: We've reached this part again. Swap. Do my usual job while I try yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We just swapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now you're worried, so the apron has followed the responsibility back.

S226.title: Become What You Compete With
S226.instruction: Turn comparison into imitation: adopt whatever quality seems powerful, allowing each borrowed trait to change the basis of the rivalry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I borrow the confident pose I was criticizing.
beats.text: Apparently this is how winners stand now. Judge me on the quality I just borrowed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said neatness didn't matter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Until it became the quality you'd chosen to compete in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I adopt the same fussy precision I mocked.
beats.text: If neatness wins, I'll become neater than you. Judge me on the quality I just borrowed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now you're copying my pose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Borrowing the current definition of victory, then improving it.

S227.title: Trust with a Trapdoor
S227.instruction: Use one person as your anchor while preserving a private condition that could reverse your trust when a recurring detail returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hand you the key but keep a backup ready.
beats.text: I trust you while that blue light stays off. Explain the condition we used to avoid saying aloud.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you trusted me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I do. The blue light wasn't part of the sentence when I said it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pull the trusted letter away at a familiar phrase.
beats.text: That word changes what I'm willing to rely on. Explain the condition we used to avoid saying aloud.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just one word.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The exact word our trust used to step carefully around.

S228.title: The Incident Keeps Changing
S228.instruction: Carry an unnamed past rupture whose meaning shifts with each new detail, while never letting its emotional weight diminish.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add a new note to the unopened incident file.
beats.text: That makes the same afternoon worse in a new way. Tell me where this new detail fits into that day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That detail changes everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The same afternoon has acquired an entirely new way to hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the old apology around without opening it.
beats.text: I thought I knew what this was apologizing for. Tell me where this new detail fits into that day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You already accepted the apology.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the version of the incident I thought had happened.

S229.title: Every Compliment Raises the Bar
S229.instruction: Treat each compliment as sincere admiration and a new standard you must immediately surpass.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I take a compliment down as a new target.
beats.text: Good at it? Then I have to be better by tomorrow. Watch one more attempt before deciding I'm impressive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can just accept a compliment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And leave today's good as tomorrow's ceiling?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move my standard above the praise just received.
beats.text: That's the new minimum, apparently. Watch one more attempt before deciding I'm impressive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That attempt was impressive too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you've given me another minimum to clear before going home.

S230.title: My Past Self Is Watching
S230.instruction: Behave as though an earlier version of yourself is judging every choice. Alternate between honoring that identity and deliberately betraying it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn my childhood photograph toward the decision.
beats.text: That version of me would be furious. Tell me which choice I would once have been proud of.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You aren't that child anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, but that child has very strong opinions about the signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I sign while covering my younger face in the photo.
beats.text: Just this once, I'm disappointing the old me on purpose. Tell me which choice I would once have been proud of.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why cover the photograph?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because I'd like to disappoint my old principles without making eye contact.

S231.title: Relief Is Suspicious
S231.instruction: Treat every reassuring development as evidence that the real threat has merely changed shape.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I inspect the reassuring note for a hidden second page.
beats.text: Too good. The bad part has learned manners. Check what this good news might be distracting us from.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's an all-clear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly where a clever danger would hide the next sentence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I prepare a backup plan after the all-clear.
beats.text: An all-clear gives danger somewhere new to hide. Check what this good news might be distracting us from.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't good news just be good?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not without explaining why it arrived so reassuringly.

S232.title: Rescue Me by Needing Me
S232.instruction: Take protective control, then let each consequence reveal how much your confidence depends on remaining necessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I take the difficult job and hold it tightly.
beats.text: I can keep you safe while you still need me. Leave me one part of the rescue to handle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can finish alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then leave me the dangerous corner. It helps me remain steady.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hover beside the task you might manage alone.
beats.text: I'd be steadier if you needed another hand. Leave me one part of the rescue to handle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You seem to need this job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone has to need me doing it. That's how rescue works both ways.

S233.title: Belonging on Changing Terms
S233.instruction: Seek acceptance by adapting quickly, then let each adaptation create a new version of yourself you must defend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I change my badge to match the new welcome rule.
beats.text: This is the version of me you invited, right? Tell me which version gets to stay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can be yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which one? I've changed badges twice to remain invited.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I defend the costume I put on moments ago.
beats.text: I can't change again; I've just become this person. Tell me which version gets to stay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was only a joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've already become the person the joke welcomed. Don't move the doorway again.

S234.title: Humility with Evidence
S234.instruction: Perform modesty while planting small facts that can later assemble themselves into undeniable proof of your importance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tuck my signature beneath the finished repair.
beats.text: Nothing special. My initials just happen to be there. Look at the little dates before praising the result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did good work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing worth mentioning beyond those six dated calls.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave dated evidence beside my modest shrug.
beats.text: It practically solved itself, after my six calls. Look at the little dates before praising the result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why put your name under it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Purely for accuracy. Modesty shouldn't make evidence disappear.

S235.title: The Ritual Explains Itself Later
S235.instruction: Treat one unexplained recurring action as essential. Allow its meaning to change each time it returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tap the cup twice before making the request.
beats.text: First it was luck. Today it's how I remember. Give me a moment to finish our unexplained little signal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why tap the cup now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because somebody used to answer with a third tap. Leave room for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I repeat the unexplained gesture more tenderly.
beats.text: Same gesture. It means something else this time. Give me a moment to finish our unexplained little signal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought that gesture meant luck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then. Today it's how I ask you to remember without explaining everything.

S236.title: The Warning Was Already Here
S236.instruction: Choose one early detail as the warning sign, then let every later development reveal a larger version of the same disaster.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I circle the first tiny crack on the old sketch.
beats.text: It warned us at the beginning; we just called it decoration. Look at the earliest warning before fixing the latest damage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The little crack seemed harmless.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why it was allowed to grow into the part we're paying for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place today's larger break beside yesterday's note.
beats.text: Same shape, much bigger cost. Look at the earliest warning before fixing the latest damage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need to fix today's break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start where yesterday tried to warn us quietly.

S237.title: Exactly the Victory I Meant
S237.instruction: Celebrate every reversal as though it secretly delivers the outcome you wanted, while preserving enthusiasm for all earlier outcomes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I change the victory sign without lowering it.
beats.text: A reversal! Exactly the surprise I hoped to win. Celebrate this version of success with me too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the opposite of what you wanted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: On the surface. Deeper down I'd prepared to celebrate surprises.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I toast the opposite result with the same enthusiasm.
beats.text: I wanted that as well, in a deeper sense. Celebrate this version of success with me too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And found out how generously I can redefine success. Raise your glass.

S238.title: Track the Cost That Returns
S238.instruction: Accept every twist, but keep returning to one practical consequence whose importance grows as the scene becomes more complicated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add another figure beside the first repair bill.
beats.text: We're still paying for that first loose screw. Deal with the original leak before announcing another miracle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Something new has happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, and the original loose screw has added another item to the bill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I bring back the same little bucket, now overflowing.
beats.text: Every twist still drips in here. Deal with the original leak before announcing another miracle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's another miracle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does this miracle empty the bucket or merely make it glow?

S239.title: The Object Changes Meaning
S239.instruction: Choose one ordinary detail and reinterpret it as gift, threat, evidence, or symbol as the scene evolves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the gifted key into a piece of evidence.
beats.text: Yesterday a welcome. Today proof I could get in. Tell me what this key means between us now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You gave me that key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As a welcome. Now it's the reason you could reach the locked drawer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the same key between us as an offer.
beats.text: It could still be an invitation instead of an accusation. Tell me what this key means between us now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I return it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Or keep it as the invitation I'm deciding whether to make again.

S240.title: The Callback Changes Meaning
S240.instruction: Treat every returning phrase or action as evidence the relationship has changed. Repeat it with a new emotional meaning each time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I repeat our old greeting without its familiar smile.
beats.text: 'Make yourself at home' used to feel different. Say the old phrase once as though we've made up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said make yourself at home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I did. Before your boxes made that sound like surrender.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I repeat the same greeting softly and slide over a cup.
beats.text: Let's try making those words kind again. Say the old phrase once as though we've made up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does it mean I can stay?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Today it means I left a clean cup for you on purpose.

D01.title: Admit You Need Me
D01.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set my toolbox just beyond the broken hinge.
beats.text: Say you need my help, and I'll open the toolbox.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need the screwdriver.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The screwdriver comes with me. Try the sentence again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave space beside my name on the repair sheet.
beats.text: Tell me which part you can't do without me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could hold the hinge myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why have you drawn my hands on the diagram?

D02.title: Don’t Go
D02.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I balance a wobbly tray near the doorway.
beats.text: Hold this for a second; I can't find its other leg.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could put it on the floor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with the farewell cake on it. Help me find a safer table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a second unopened envelope.
beats.text: Read this one before you put your coat on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This one is empty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we should search for the missing letter before you go.

D03.title: Say You’re Sorry
D03.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the dented cup between us in silence.
beats.text: Is there anything you'd like to say before we use this again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It still holds tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. What a remarkably forgiving cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I begin a note with 'I am...' and pass it across.
beats.text: Finish that sentence however your conscience suggests.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I am hungry?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting that your stomach has found words before your conscience.

D04.title: Retroactive Permission
D04.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold out the receipt without showing the total.
beats.text: Say the new sign is approved; it's already hanging outside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You bought it before asking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I left the ribbon uncut. You still get the grand approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stand in front of a freshly painted door.
beats.text: Agree that yellow was the right choice before you look behind me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You painted my front door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the outside. There's still plenty for you to authorize.

D05.title: Make It Their Idea
D05.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I display a new label on the rubbish bag.
beats.text: Who wants the prestigious role of final quality inspection outside?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That sounds like taking out the rubbish.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With exclusive access to the courtyard. I can't offer that to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I polish the only handle on the cleaning cart.
beats.text: Volunteer for the job with your very own set of wheels.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those wheels are on a mop bucket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Most promotions don't include a vehicle.

D06.title: How Much Do You Know?
D06.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I mention only the first letter on the envelope.
beats.text: Which version of yesterday's story have you heard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which story are you worried about?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: None. I'm deciding which one deserves correcting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I open a blank page as though checking old notes.
beats.text: Start from the bit you know, and I'll fill in only what's necessary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tell me what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd rather not contaminate your very valuable recollection.

D07.title: Join Me
D07.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide half a secret map across the table.
beats.text: Meet me at the back gate; I'll explain the other half there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why only half a map?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The other half has your job on it. Are you coming?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave a folded invitation beneath a cup.
beats.text: Take this as an invitation to something we won't announce yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no event name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's working. Bring shoes you can leave quietly in.

D08.title: You First
D08.instruction: Coax someone else into breaking a rule before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the 'do not open' label.
beats.text: Try the handle first; I'll watch what happens.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The label says not to open it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only one of us needs to check whether that's still necessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep my own pen capped above the forbidden line.
beats.text: Cross that line on your form before I cross mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why won't you sign first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because someone responsible should remain available to explain.

D09.title: Recognize Me
D09.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your importance, expertise, or authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to my small name at the bottom.
beats.text: Say who actually solved the problem before we move on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were going to thank the whole team.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The whole team watched me fix it. They can start the applause.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place my tool beside the completed repair.
beats.text: Introduce me as the person who made this work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you helped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Say it into the microphone this time.

D10.title: Choose Me
D10.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move my invitation beside the competing one.
beats.text: Pick my evening, not the one you've nearly agreed to.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already promised I'd go there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your favourite dessert beside your place here. It doesn't travel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I bring my chair level with the alternative seat.
beats.text: Choose this seat beside me for once.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can see both of you from over here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but which of us gets your coat on their chair?

D11.title: Prove Your Loyalty
D11.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put two differently coloured cups out.
beats.text: Which cup would you choose if nobody were scoring your answer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does the colour matter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not at all. I simply noticed how quickly you chose blue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave an inconvenient note by the door.
beats.text: Keep this tiny favour between us, just to see how that feels.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I ask Sam to help?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. It's useful to know how private your private favours are.

D12.title: Give It Up
D12.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold open a small empty box.
beats.text: Put the medal in here; let it be mine for this part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only medal I've won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why a paper replica wouldn't mean the same thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a receipt for an object I'm not holding yet.
beats.text: Hand over the key without needing to keep a spare.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I always keep a spare.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're lending me a key, not giving up the door.

D13.title: Helpful Culprit
D13.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hide my glue-stained thumb behind a clipboard.
beats.text: Let me investigate the broken vase, starting far away from the glue.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is there glue on your thumb?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent observation. I'll investigate the stationery cupboard personally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover my muddy footprint with the evidence tray.
beats.text: Check the windows first; I'm sure the culprit came from outside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That footprint matches your boot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the intruder had impeccable taste. Let's measure the window.

D14.title: Not That Subject
D14.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the damaged photograph facedown.
beats.text: Before we discuss the photograph, have we ordered lunch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who tore the photograph?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll need two menus. I can't discuss anything while you're hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pick up a spoon beside the incriminating note.
beats.text: Forget that note for a moment; who polished these spoons?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The note says you cancelled it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And it was written with a dirty pen. Who's managing the cleaning supplies?

D15.title: Merciful Lie
D15.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover the rejection letter with a cheerful postcard.
beats.text: There's no news you need to worry about today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does that say rejected?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It says they can't imagine a replacement for you. That's almost the same.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I fold the broken invitation into my pocket.
beats.text: The change of plans is only about the weather, honestly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's sunny outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're worried about tomorrow. Weather is very forward-thinking.

D16.title: Confess First
D16.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep my own signed note folded shut.
beats.text: Tell me what you did first; then I'll open my envelope.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You promised to tell me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will. Your confession establishes the appropriate level of detail.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw two confession columns and leave mine blank.
beats.text: Start with your mistake so I know how honest we're being.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is your column still empty?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm leaving enough room to match your honesty.

D17.title: Sell the Disaster
D17.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place a bucket beneath a drawing of a roofless room.
beats.text: A missing roof saves a fortune on ventilation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain will come straight in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And straight out of the cleaning budget. Two problems solved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I label the least safe route 'efficient'.
beats.text: Approve this shortcut; risk is just unused efficiency.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bridge isn't finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll be the first across. Imagine the time that saves.

D18.title: Fake the Expertise
D18.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I adjust an unfamiliar dial with enormous confidence.
beats.text: That hum means it's calibrating; I prefer not to interrupt it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The smoke is new.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the machine's way of displaying progress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I inspect the underside of the instruction manual.
beats.text: The upside-down test is standard in advanced work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're reading the French section.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An expert checks the machine's second language too.

D19.title: Everything Is a Contest
D19.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put a timer beside the disagreement.
beats.text: Let's settle this by seeing who finishes first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We disagree about dinner, not speed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First one to peel five potatoes chooses the restaurant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move two cups to an imaginary starting line.
beats.text: Pick a side; even pouring tea can establish a winner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we just drink the tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When one of us has proved we pour more accurately.

D20.title: Brighter Side
D20.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smile at an empty cupboard.
beats.text: Perfect, now we know exactly how much room we've got.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no food either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then every shelf is available for a fresh start.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold up the broken handle like a prize.
beats.text: Wonderful, one less thing that can stick tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we can't open the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Finally, uninterrupted time together.

D21.title: Supportive Rage
D21.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smooth a crumpled napkin with rigid fingers.
beats.text: Lovely choice; I'll happily fix the extra mess myself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you also wipe the floor?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. My knees were hoping to join in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer another cup through a tight smile.
beats.text: Take your time; my entire afternoon is yours, apparently.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I might take another hour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I'll just reschedule the entire afternoon inside my head.

D22.title: Terms and Conditions
D22.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I write a price beside a friendly favour.
beats.text: I'll lend the ladder for two future lifts home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need it for five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then one lift home and a favourable mention at dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add a signature line to a verbal apology.
beats.text: Your apology is accepted once we agree what it includes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you just accept I'm sorry?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The words are fine. We're negotiating the warranty.

D23.title: Yes, but My Way
D23.instruction: Agree with others, then reinterpret the agreement entirely in your favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tick 'attend' but leave 'help' blank.
beats.text: Yes, I'll be there; I never agreed to carry anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you'd help set up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I am helping attendance. Look how present I am.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I underline one convenient word in our agreement.
beats.text: Absolutely, I'll help with the first box; the rest weren't specified.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are twenty boxes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I was very specific about my enthusiasm for the first.

D24.title: The Pattern
D24.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I connect two tiny stains on a map.
beats.text: One spill is clumsy; two reveal a whole operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those are coffee rings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two drinks abandoned. Someone is rushing the entire operation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add a squeaking chair to a growing diagram.
beats.text: Hear that squeak? Even the furniture is part of this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs oil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what they want you to think about every warning.

D25.title: Could You Just…
D25.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a single loose screw, then the whole bracket.
beats.text: Could you just hold this, then tighten it, then finish the shelf?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm already holding up the whole shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Just pop those books on while you're there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set one envelope on top of a large unsorted pile.
beats.text: Start with this tiny letter; the rest use the same easy process.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are fifty letters underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once you've learned the process, stopping wastes all that experience.

D26.title: One Last Thing
D26.instruction: Keep someone present by discovering one more small task, question, or favor whenever departure seems near.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stop packing after spotting another cup.
beats.text: Before you go, there's just this one cup to rinse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've washed it. Goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Now the cupboard door is sticking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I reach for the last bag as a coat goes on.
beats.text: Wait, this knot needs a second pair of hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. The knot's open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you check whether anything fell out? You've got the best view.

D27.title: You Could at Least…
D27.instruction: Make the inconvenience visible enough that an apology becomes the easiest way forward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I peel a wet sock off very slowly.
beats.text: The puddle you left has had quite an afternoon with my foot.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you won't mind holding this sock through dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the ruined timetable beside my untouched dinner.
beats.text: Three missed buses; perhaps there's a word for what I deserve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You still got home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just in time to watch my dinner solidify. What do we say?

D28.title: Just Say Yes
D28.instruction: Get a quick approval before anyone has time to examine the practical consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover the small print with my thumb.
beats.text: Just say yes to the first line; we'll discuss the rest later.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I should read all of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, after the yes. Reading takes longer than approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold a stamp above the request.
beats.text: A quick nod is enough before you read the expensive part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What does it cost?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A hesitation costs us the offer. Shall I stamp it?

D29.title: Your Turn
D29.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the cleaning rota beside the mop.
beats.text: Your name has been beside this task since Monday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you enjoyed mopping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I enjoy seeing my name removed from this column.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the last four completed chores toward you.
beats.text: I've done my turns; this bucket is yours now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did this last month.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You'll remember where the bucket lives.

D30.title: What Was the Plan?
D30.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I examine an empty calendar as though checking it.
beats.text: Remind me which time we settled on, just for the record.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We agreed on four. Did you forget?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking whether you remembered the same four.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold two conflicting lists.
beats.text: Which list did we agree was the final plan?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sent both of these.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Which one sounded most final when I sent it?

D31.title: Back Me Up
D31.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put my version of the rota next to yours.
beats.text: Back me up when I say the bins were never my turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't remember agreeing with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remember me sounding very convincing, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a copy of the household note.
beats.text: Tell them you remember the arrangement the way I do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That isn't how it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's agree on the useful version before the meeting.

D32.title: Try It First
D32.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hand over the questionable replacement part.
beats.text: Try the cheaper fitting first; I'll stand well back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it leaks?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll have learned something without wetting my shoes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep my own cup away from the experimental tap.
beats.text: Taste the water after the repair before I fill mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why aren't you drinking yours?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone needs a clear palate for the comparison.

D33.title: Count What I Did
D33.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I spread the shopping receipts across the table.
beats.text: Count the trips on these before calling this a small favour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were going out anyway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not up these six flights, twice, carrying your soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I line up the bags by the stairs.
beats.text: Notice how many flights I carried every one of these up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thanks for bringing them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you include the stairs in that sentence?

D34.title: Pick a Priority
D34.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put a late parcel beside the ringing phone.
beats.text: Choose the delivery or the call; both supposedly come first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you do both?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can answer the phone holding it. Which one do I drop?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold the dinner timer beside the departure ticket.
beats.text: Pick what burns: the dinner or the timetable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Dinner's nearly ready.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're deciding between hungry and late. Pick one aloud.

D35.title: Move It for Me
D35.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pencil my name into your busy calendar.
beats.text: Move that ordinary appointment so we can have this hour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's my weekly appointment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. It happens every week. I'm asking for one of them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I lay my invitation across another commitment.
beats.text: Reschedule one thing for me, not because it's convenient.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: But I already said yes elsewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'm asking whether your yes to me can move anything.

D36.title: Hand It Over
D36.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold out both hands beside the struggling repair.
beats.text: Give me the hinge before we turn one loose screw into three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've almost fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're holding the loose end. Let me take the piece attached to the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put my empty clipboard beside the unfinished plan.
beats.text: Hand me the planning for this part and step back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to lose control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then delegate the mistakes to me. Start with that clipboard.

D37.title: Put It Back Quietly
D37.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide the borrowed pen back into its cup.
beats.text: Was that pen ever missing? It looks perfectly at home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's not my pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lighting in this room changes everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I replace a cracked plate with a similar one.
beats.text: The cupboard always had this pattern, more or less.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our plates never had flowers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A pattern can grow on you surprisingly quickly.

D38.title: Talk Around the Mess
D38.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I align labels in front of the unsorted mess.
beats.text: Before we discuss the missed cleanup, which label colour looks best?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The room still needs cleaning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why choosing the correct labels is so important.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I polish one spoon beside a mountain of plates.
beats.text: Look at this shine; let's start with what's going well.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What about all the plates?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's appreciate one completed object before crushing morale.

D39.title: Spare Them the Hassle
D39.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slip the repair bill into my own bag.
beats.text: Nothing you need to deal with; I've already made the call.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is that our address on the invoice?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just a minor detail I've already volunteered to manage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I quietly place a bucket under the leak.
beats.text: Go enjoy lunch; the extra water is my little project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Water's coming through the ceiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll use the larger bucket. Enjoy lunch.

D40.title: Who Changed It?
D40.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to a chair moved from its usual place.
beats.text: Who had a reason to put this here yesterday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I moved it to reach the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And was that before or after the timetable changed?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I compare two versions of the schedule.
beats.text: Which pen wrote the new time, out of curiosity?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's my pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting. Did the pen choose six o'clock by itself?

D41.title: Basically Finished
D41.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover the unfinished corner with a decorative cloth.
beats.text: The uncovered part is complete; the rest is intentional breathing room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no paint under that cloth.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's an optional viewing area.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tape a note over the missing handle.
beats.text: It's finished as a prototype of simplicity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do we open it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: By appreciating how little clutter is left on the front.

D42.title: I’ve Done This Before
D42.instruction: Perform calm familiarity with the task while learning how it works from every new clue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I inspect the unusual latch while nodding.
beats.text: Yes, this model always opens differently from the one before.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You pull, not push.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I was checking the resistance before the pull.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I read a fresh instruction as though recalling it.
beats.text: Of course, turn it clockwise; exactly what I was about to do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said anticlockwise a moment ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was the diagnostic direction. Now we use the working direction.

D43.title: Outdo the Effort
D43.instruction: Answer every favor, chore, or sacrifice with a bigger one that restores your lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add another bag to the favour already offered.
beats.text: You carried two? I'll carry four and make the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to carry all that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. That's what makes it more generous.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I rewrite my task list to be longer.
beats.text: Your generous hour deserves my entire afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was just trying to help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'm helping so thoroughly you can take tomorrow off too.

D44.title: Efficiency Win
D44.instruction: Celebrate each inconvenience as proof that a faster, cheaper, or smarter routine can now be invented.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I celebrate the lift breaking.
beats.text: Excellent, the stairs will solve our exercise problem too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We live on the eighth floor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we've cancelled eight gym memberships in one afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I count the coins saved by a cancelled trip.
beats.text: A delay and a budget improvement in one afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We missed the wedding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And look, enough savings to send a genuinely impressive card.

D45.title: No Trouble at All
D45.instruction: Remain gracious and accommodating while making your growing inconvenience impossible to miss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smile while dragging the unexpectedly heavy bag.
beats.text: No trouble at all; I only needed that shoulder for the rest of my life.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can carry it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, now? After it's learned the shape of my shoulder?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add another place setting with careful politeness.
beats.text: Another guest is lovely; my portion was optional anyway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you sure there's enough dinner?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the guest, certainly. I've always admired restraint.

D46.title: Fair Exchange
D46.instruction: Price every favor in time, effort, inconvenience, or future obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I mark thirty minutes beside the favour.
beats.text: Half an hour now buys me your Saturday morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Saturday is my only free morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you appreciate the value of these thirty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put two household tasks on a balance sheet.
beats.text: I'll do the dishes if you do the next two grocery runs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two shopping trips for one wash-up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This pan has dried cheese. The exchange rate has changed.

D47.title: Technically, Yes
D47.instruction: Comply with every agreement in the narrowest possible way while insisting you honored it completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I carry one tiny box from the enormous pile.
beats.text: You asked me to move a box. Done.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant all the boxes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll enjoy making a wonderfully precise second request.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I water the single plant named in the request.
beats.text: The others weren't included in 'water that one'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The others are wilting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A tragedy outside the scope of my assignment.

D48.title: One Thing Leads to Another
D48.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I enlarge a repair diagram until it covers the table.
beats.text: Fixing the tap means we should redesign the entire kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We only need a washer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but what kind of kitchen deserves that washer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move from one loose chair leg to every chair.
beats.text: We can't solve this properly without replacing all the seating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The others are fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They share a manufacturer. We must investigate the whole family.

D49.title: Make Them Your Deputy
D49.instruction: Get someone’s help by defining it as service under your direction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I write 'deputy' on a spare badge.
beats.text: Help me by taking this assignment under my direction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather share the job equally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You will. Equally with the other people following my instructions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place a small chair beside my larger one.
beats.text: Join the operation as my reliable second.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is mine lower?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So you can see the plan from the operational level.

D50.title: Not Dismissed
D50.instruction: Keep someone present by treating departure as a privilege only you can grant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep the dismissal line on the form blank.
beats.text: You can collect your coat when I release you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My shift ended ten minutes ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And your release is coming along beautifully. Sit down while I review it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold the exit note without signing it.
beats.text: Departure is pending my approval, not your timetable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't need permission to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this should be a very easy form for you to wait for.

D51.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
D51.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place my title above the disputed sentence.
beats.text: Apologize for speaking to my position that way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry the plan failed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The plan can wait. Address the rank you interrupted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the courtesy crossed out in the note.
beats.text: The incident matters less than the respect you skipped.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I disagreed with an idea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Using my first name. Let's repair that part first.

D52.title: Secure the Endorsement
D52.instruction: Get a visible endorsement that makes your decision or position harder to challenge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold a supporting statement beside the microphone.
beats.text: Endorse this decision where everyone can hear you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you privately I liked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Privately won't reach the microphone. Shall I adjust the height?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide the public approval page forward.
beats.text: Put your name on the support line so it can't vanish later.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I support it anonymously?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if Anonymous will stand beside me for the photograph.

D53.title: Delegate Downward
D53.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw an arrow from my job to yours.
beats.text: This unpleasant job travels down the chart to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That arrow wasn't there yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We update procedures as responsibilities become unpleasant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the task beneath a subordinate title.
beats.text: Accept this as the junior responsibility it plainly is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're passing down all the bad jobs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm giving you a very complete picture of junior leadership.

D54.title: Find the Real Authority
D54.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I trace the final approval line.
beats.text: Who can actually stop this after everybody else agrees?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone has already signed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Who can make those signatures stop counting?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I lay three signatures side by side.
beats.text: Which one of these could reverse the other two?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're equally important.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whose phone call would make us put the papers away?

D55.title: Build a Coalition
D55.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add an empty chair to my side of the table.
beats.text: Sit with me so this looks like more than one person's opinion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not sure I agree.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can sit on my side while you work that out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave a supporting name blank on the proposal.
beats.text: Join the proposal before they call it my private campaign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't read it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put your name in pencil. We can discuss permanence after the vote.

D56.title: Challenge by Proxy
D56.instruction: Persuade someone else to challenge a rule or authority before you risk doing it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pass over a complaint I haven't signed.
beats.text: Ask the chair why that rule exists before I risk asking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you ask the chair?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd hate my position to distract from your excellent question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the forbidden shortcut from a safe distance.
beats.text: Challenge the restriction first; I'll support the result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you stand beside me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Behind you. Close enough to be supportive, far enough to remain useful.

D57.title: Use the Proper Title
D57.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tap the full name on my badge.
beats.text: Use the title when you introduce me, not just the first name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sure, Pat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Director Pat. The first syllables do most of the work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I straighten the place card with my rank.
beats.text: Give me the courtesy that comes with this position.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just an informal dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then a quiet, affectionate 'Director' should feel perfectly natural.

D58.title: Declare Allegiance
D58.instruction: Make someone choose which person, side, or claim to authority they will support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put two rival proposals in front of you.
beats.text: Choose whose authority you're going to support.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I support parts of both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose whose signature you want above those parts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer two coloured ribbons.
beats.text: Wear one side's colour; neutrality isn't an answer I can use.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I wear neither?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll know which side refused to wear mine.
