D59.title: Obey Without Explanation
D59.instruction: Create increasingly inconvenient requests that test whether someone accepts your authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place a trivial object across the room.
beats.text: Bring that here without needing me to justify the request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why do you need it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm interested in the part where you do it without the explanation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the object again after its return.
beats.text: Now take it back; I'm checking something other than distance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: But you just asked me to bring it here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now we discover whether that was a one-time achievement.

D60.title: Pass Me the Authority
D60.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold out the official key.
beats.text: Name me as the next decision-maker before you hand it over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I simply give you the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The door knows what a key means. I'd like the room to know too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave the chair empty for a public announcement.
beats.text: Tell the room the authority passes to me now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone can see you're sitting there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then saying I'm in charge should require very little imagination.

D61.title: Orders from the Shadows
D61.instruction: Hide that you set the problem in motion while quietly directing how everyone responds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hide the original instruction beneath the response plan.
beats.text: Follow this new direction; there's no need to discuss who started it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This problem began with your order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why my corrective order is so well informed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I quietly remove my initials from the first order.
beats.text: Let's concentrate on my solution, not the missing signature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: These erased letters look like your initials.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's spend our attention on the much clearer letters in my solution.

D62.title: Not Up for Debate
D62.instruction: Keep the conversation from examining where your authority comes from or whether it is legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn my appointment letter facedown.
beats.text: Who appointed me is outside today's discussion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who actually appointed you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can schedule that discussion after you've finished these tasks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set a task list over the question of credentials.
beats.text: We'll debate the job, not my right to assign it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd like to see your certificate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to see today's work. One of those is more urgent.

D63.title: For Stability’s Sake
D63.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I remove a destabilizing page from the briefing.
beats.text: The shortened version will keep everyone steady.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where is the last page?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It contains information that would make today's simple job complicated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the alarming note in a sealed drawer.
beats.text: The leadership is stable enough for today's purposes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is the director resigning?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chair will remain in exactly the same place.

D64.title: Name Your Backers
D64.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add blank spaces beside an authorization.
beats.text: Name who backed you before we talk about the decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I made the decision myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who made it safe for you to make that decision?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the invisible chain behind a signature.
beats.text: Who benefits from letting you give that order?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My name is right there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Whose name would you mention if this went wrong?

D65.title: Strategic Retreat
D65.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I surrender the best chair with elaborate calm.
beats.text: I chose to give up that position; strategic generosity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were voted out of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I gave the vote a practical opportunity to express itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move my marker backward as though planned.
beats.text: Retreat creates room for my influence to expand later.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're moving backward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Influence needs a running start.

D66.title: Act Authorized
D66.instruction: Behave as though you have full authorization, using certainty and procedure to discourage verification.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I display an unsigned pass without pausing.
beats.text: The permission is in order; let's not slow down to verify it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's been approved at the level where signatures become unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stamp my own request confidently.
beats.text: Authorization has already been handled, as you can see.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That is your own stamp.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Then we've identified the approving authority.

D67.title: Rank Everything
D67.instruction: Turn every new contribution into a ranking that places you nearer the top.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I arrange contributions from top to bottom.
beats.text: Mine goes above that one for strategic importance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're all helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm simply recording the order in which we'd collapse without us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add a ranking column to a friendly suggestion list.
beats.text: Helpfulness is good, but who was most essential?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Do we need a winner?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not a winner. A most-essential contributor. I've added a column.

D68.title: More Power, More Problems
D68.instruction: Celebrate every burden, restriction, or crisis as evidence that your influence is expanding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I grin at the enormous pile of new problems.
beats.text: So many problems must mean they trust my power.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've cut your budget again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They clearly expect me to achieve the impossible. Recognition at last.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pin another responsibility onto my badge.
beats.text: Another restriction means another boundary worth controlling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've lost access to two rooms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which makes the remaining room my undisputed headquarters.

D69.title: Gracious Command
D69.instruction: Remain warm and appreciative while steadily reducing everyone else’s room to choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smile while crossing options off the list.
beats.text: Thank you for choosing; I've narrowed your options to the correct one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There isn't a choice left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And thank you for saving us the delay of choosing badly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer an appreciative handshake over a strict instruction.
beats.text: I'm grateful for your flexibility about having no alternative.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't agree to this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I appreciate how honestly you're beginning your cooperation.

D70.title: Access Has a Price
D70.instruction: Turn every piece of access, information, or approval into a favor, debt, or condition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep a door key beside an IOU.
beats.text: Access costs a favour I can name later.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just go through the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can. We'll decide what you owe once you've enjoyed the access.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I lift a useful page just out of the stack.
beats.text: One approval buys one introduction; let's be precise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if I have nothing to offer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we can admire the closed door together.

D71.title: Consensus Means Me
D71.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I mark a hesitant nod as support on the chart.
beats.text: I'll record that as agreement with my leadership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only nodded at the date.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A leadership programme needs a date. You've approved the foundation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place 'unanimous' over two qualified comments.
beats.text: Your agreement on the date confirms the whole plan under me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I objected to half of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which leaves an uncontested half for my announcement.

D72.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
D72.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw my boundary around the latest problem.
beats.text: That affects my area, so I'll need to control this part too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The kitchen isn't your department.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It supplies my department's tea. That's a strategic connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add another key to my ring.
beats.text: One more responsibility requires one more room under my authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why do you need the roof key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Rain reaches my window. I need oversight at the source.

D73.title: Be There for Me
D73.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set out an extra cup beside the task.
beats.text: Show up for this, not because it's easy, but because it's us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could hire someone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I could. They wouldn't remember why this table matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave room for another pair of hands.
beats.text: Help with this one thing so I know we're still connected.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not good at this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay beside me and be bad at it together.

D74.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
D74.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold my coat without putting it on.
beats.text: Before either of us leaves, tell me whether we're actually okay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We already finished cleaning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The room is tidy. I'm asking about us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I reopen a practical task that's already finished.
beats.text: The dishes are done, but we haven't settled what happened between us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's nothing left to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we finally have time to say whether we're okay.

D75.title: Name What It Cost
D75.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the missed-event ticket between us.
beats.text: Acknowledge what it cost me to stand there alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said I was sorry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me what you think I did while the seat stayed empty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the date I stopped writing.
beats.text: Tell me you understand why that silence hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone died.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking what it felt like on my side, not what happened to the battery.

D76.title: I Need Your Blessing
D76.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I show the signed decision as though unsigned.
beats.text: I don't need permission, but I still need your blessing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've already chosen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Now I need to hear your voice sound happy about it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer the good news without smiling yet.
beats.text: Say you're glad I chose this before I celebrate it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why aren't you celebrating?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm waiting to learn whether this is good news to both of us.

D77.title: Carry This with Me
D77.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move half the difficult papers toward you.
beats.text: Carry part of this because we're not supposed to do it alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You know more about this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know enough to be tired. Take one page because you're here with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put another handle on the heavy bag.
beats.text: Take this side as part of being in my life.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't pack it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Neither did I, alone. That second handle is part of the relationship.

D78.title: What Are We Now?
D78.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hover over the label on an invitation.
beats.text: What should I put beside your name for us?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just write my name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a box after the name. I keep looking at that box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave two seats together on the plan.
beats.text: Would we sit together at something neither of us organized?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could sit wherever.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what strangers say when they don't want to commit to a table.

D79.title: Take My Side
D79.instruction: Recruit someone into your interpretation of a conflict involving a shared relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pass you my account of the old argument.
beats.text: Back my version when the family story gets told.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember it differently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could your memory stand beside mine while they're all listening?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I mark the part where our memories diverge.
beats.text: Take my side about what that promise meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left out what you said.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll add my part after they understand why your part supports me.

examples.transferProp: the note recording our disputed promise

D80.title: Prove We’re Close
D80.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a private note without letting go.
beats.text: Say something unguarded with me, just once.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone might read it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say the sentence to me instead of leaving it on paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold the invitation we'd usually decline.
beats.text: Come as my guest even if somebody asks what we are.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: People will ask questions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let them ask. Could we give one honest answer together?

D81.title: Acknowledge Our History
D81.instruction: Make someone recognize that the relationship, memory, or sacrifice mattered and cannot be treated as incidental.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn our oldest photograph toward you.
beats.text: Say this mattered before putting it in storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just a picture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say what you remember before I let it become just paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I display the worn ticket from our first trip.
beats.text: Don't call this a random souvenir; tell me what it was to us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You keep everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the things I need someone else to confirm mattered.

D82.title: Choose the Relationship
D82.instruction: Make someone prioritize this connection over a competing person, promise, or opportunity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put my invitation next to the promotion letter.
beats.text: Choose a little time with me over the impressive opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This opportunity won't come twice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Neither will tonight. I've already set your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave a seat beside me while a phone rings.
beats.text: Stay with this conversation instead of taking that call.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's important.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choosing to leave it ringing would mean something.

D83.title: Remember Me Correctly
D83.instruction: Create small tests of whether someone remembers your preferences, stories, or shared history.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set out three drinks without labelling mine.
beats.text: Which one would you have poured for me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't remember which you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's all right. It is only something I told you every morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I stop midway through an old story.
beats.text: Finish the part you used to remember better than I did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which part comes next?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The part you used to interrupt me to tell yourself.

D84.title: Let Go of the Grudge
D84.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender resentment, distance, or a claim that keeps the relationship stuck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the apology note beside a fresh invitation.
beats.text: Leave the old claim here and come to the next dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not ready to forget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the memory. Leave the demand for payment off the dinner table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold out an empty box for the saved grievance.
beats.text: Give up this one piece of the argument so we can move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why should I give that up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because carrying it takes the hand I'd like you to offer me.

D85.title: I Pulled Away First
D85.instruction: Hide your role in creating the distance while working urgently to repair it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hide the unanswered letters under fresh stationery.
beats.text: Let's reconnect without counting who stopped writing first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You stopped answering first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And look at this lovely blank stationery where we could start again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a new key while covering the old changed lock.
beats.text: I've missed us; the lock is just a practical detail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why was my old key useless?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Locks age. Could we talk about how nice it is to have you back?

D86.title: Not Why We Drifted
D86.instruction: Keep the conversation away from the real reason the relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I change the topic from the old silence to dinner.
beats.text: Let's talk about what to cook, not why I disappeared.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where were you for six months?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did we still like the same soup six months ago?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the cheerful part of the photograph.
beats.text: Remember the weather that day, not the conversation afterward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the day you disappeared.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And such impossible sunshine. Look at the shadows.

D87.title: Keep the Peace
D87.instruction: Hide a truth because you believe the relationship cannot survive one more conflict.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the new upsetting letter under an old card.
beats.text: There's nothing new worth reopening the argument for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was there another message?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing that belongs at this peaceful breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I straighten the table over a hidden message.
beats.text: Today can stay peaceful with the shorter explanation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're hiding something under the cloth.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the sort of detail that would ruin the meal before it starts.

D88.title: Say You Missed Me
D88.instruction: Get someone to admit longing, jealousy, hurt, or attachment before you reveal your own.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave my own emotional note folded.
beats.text: Did you notice how quiet it was without me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you miss me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking about the noise level here first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I ask about the empty chair instead of my absence.
beats.text: Tell me whether anybody missed the noise from this seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could hear the clock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And did that feel restful or a little too quiet?

D89.title: We Needed the Break
D89.instruction: Frame a rupture, absence, or failed connection as a healthy decision that ultimately helped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I frame the gap in our calendar with a pen.
beats.text: The time apart was probably the healthiest thing we ever did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We didn't speak for a year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A full year of learning how much we had to say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn a failed reunion into a planning note.
beats.text: We needed that disastrous meeting to understand what to change.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You called it a disaster.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A disaster with excellent diagnostic value.

D90.title: I Know How to Fix Us
D90.instruction: Perform confidence about repairing the relationship while improvising every step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I produce a relationship repair list I've just invented.
beats.text: I've got a method: first tea, then whichever apology comes naturally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made that up just now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All good methods begin somewhere. Sugar is step three.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I number three blank steps confidently.
beats.text: We're on step two of fixing us; I know what comes after this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What comes after step two?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We discover what step two has made possible. Very advanced work.

D91.title: Who Cares More?
D91.instruction: Turn every favor, memory, sacrifice, and affectionate gesture into evidence that you care more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add another old ticket to the affection pile.
beats.text: I kept twelve souvenirs; how many did you keep?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't keep tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then how will we measure who's cherished this more?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I insist on taking the heavier bag.
beats.text: Let me show who cares enough to carry more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me carry something.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not the heaviest thing. I haven't finished proving a point with my spine.

D92.title: Still a Good Sign
D92.instruction: Treat every awkward or disappointing interaction as proof that the connection remains alive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smile at a painfully awkward familiar joke.
beats.text: We can still make this awkward together; that's a good sign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was painful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But familiar pain. We haven't lost our shared language.

examples.transferProp: the old joke on a napkin

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep the invitation after a postponement.
beats.text: A delay isn't a no; we've still got an invitation between us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the third cancellation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three chances to make the eventual yes spectacular.

D93.title: Affectionate Resentment
D93.instruction: Remain warm and familiar while letting old resentment sharpen beneath every caring gesture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer the favourite drink with a pointed smile.
beats.text: Here, exactly how you like it; I remember the little things.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You remembered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone had to keep the memory department open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I straighten the blanket rather sharply.
beats.text: Comfortable? I always make sure one of us is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're pulling it too tight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I would hate for you to experience an unmet need.

D94.title: Relationship Ledger
D94.instruction: Price closeness, forgiveness, and support in favors, sacrifices, access, and future loyalty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I write a future favour beside 'forgiven'.
beats.text: This apology buys one fresh start; I'll need loyalty in return.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought forgiveness was a gift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It is. The attendance requirement is simply the ribbon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I exchange the old grievance for a promise.
beats.text: I'll let that go if you'll show up next time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if I can't come next time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we should discuss the terms before I release the grievance.

examples.transferProp: the promise written inside the card

D95.title: Closer on My Terms
D95.instruction: Agree to repair the relationship while redefining closeness around the boundaries that benefit you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw a careful boundary around the reunion date.
beats.text: Yes to reconnecting; no to discussing the parts I closed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need to talk about why you left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can start with what time I'm leaving tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I accept the invitation but cross out the overnight stay.
beats.text: We can be close in the ways that let me leave at ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's not much of a visit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It is exactly the amount I can promise sincerely.

D96.title: Here We Go Again
D96.instruction: Use every new disagreement to prove the same relationship pattern is repeating, then raise the consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put today's complaint next to the old one.
beats.text: Here it is again; this time I won't rebuild the whole routine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This time is different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then name the part we'll change before using the same apology.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I circle the repeated phrase on two different notes.
beats.text: Same promise, larger consequence if it fails again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't believe me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I believe you said it. I'm deciding what happens if I hear it again.

D97.title: Let Me Lean
D97.instruction: Get someone to carry part of the emotional burden without making you name how heavy it has become.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set one heavy folder near the other chair.
beats.text: Take this one call off my hands without making me explain why.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's wrong?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please let the call be the thing you take from me first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pass over the unopened letter.
beats.text: Read the first line for me; I can't be the first to see it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want me to read it aloud?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just the first line. I'll decide whether I can hold the rest.

D98.title: Stay Until I’m Steady
D98.instruction: Keep someone present until you feel steady enough to face what comes next without them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep two cups out after the tea is finished.
beats.text: Sit through one more cup while my hands stop shaking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've had three already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we know exactly how to make a fourth.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I count my breaths with the coat still folded.
beats.text: Give me another quiet minute before the door closes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The taxi is outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let it be outside for one more breath. Count this one with me.

D99.title: Understand the Hurt
D99.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the empty seat in the photograph.
beats.text: Understand that it hurt because I saved that place for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You knew I was busy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I knew. I still watched that seat through the entire performance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set an unread message beside the apology.
beats.text: Say you understand why the silence mattered, not just that it happened.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I apologized for not replying.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me what you think I heard in that silence.

D100.title: Tell Me I Did Enough
D100.instruction: Get someone to reassure you that your effort, choice, or survival was enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I spread the work beside the rejection letter.
beats.text: Tell me that what I managed was enough.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could try harder next time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before next time, could this time count for something?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the smallest finished piece in front of you.
beats.text: Say this counts even if it wasn't everything I hoped.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It isn't the full set.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know every missing piece. Tell me what you can see in this one.

D101.title: Start the Hard Part
D101.instruction: Get someone else to explain, announce, or begin the emotionally difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide the difficult announcement across.
beats.text: You say the cancellation aloud; I'll handle the papers afterward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're the organizer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why I'll be very busy holding the list while you say it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer the telephone instead of picking it up.
beats.text: Begin the hard conversation for me; I'll join once it's started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They asked to speak to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce the subject first. I'll take over after the word 'cancelled'.

D102.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
D102.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn an unfinished answer toward the light.
beats.text: What belongs after that careful pause?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There isn't anything after the pause.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say the sentence without stopping in that exact place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave space beneath a polished explanation.
beats.text: Tell me the part that didn't fit your safe version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the whole story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's room on the page for the part you keep calling a detail.

D103.title: Hope with Me
D103.instruction: Recruit someone into believing that the outcome can still change, even when the evidence is thin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw a second route around the blocked one.
beats.text: Believe with me that there is still a way through.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That road is closed too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then draw a third with me. I can't be the only pencil moving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set two empty glasses beside the unlikely good news.
beats.text: Help me plan a celebration before all the evidence arrives.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We haven't heard back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Help me choose what we're hoping to toast.

D104.title: Say the Scary Part
D104.instruction: Get someone else to name the frightening possibility or vulnerable feeling before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave a frightening sentence half-written.
beats.text: Say the worst possibility first so I don't have to name it alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to frighten you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm frightened by the blank. Give it a name I can hear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I push the unopened result toward the other seat.
beats.text: Tell me what we're both afraid this might say.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We shouldn't guess.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then name the possibility you're working so hard not to guess.

D105.title: See What This Took
D105.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the unsent angry letter beside the polite one.
beats.text: Notice how much restraint it took to send the shorter version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm glad you calmed down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read the crossing-out. That's where all the work happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I show the first shaky draft.
beats.text: See the courage it took me to finish even this much.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only two sentences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Those were two sentences I couldn't say yesterday.

D106.title: Choose What Matters More
D106.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set the safe plan beside the ambitious one.
beats.text: Choose whether feeling safe or getting there matters more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want both safety and the opportunity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me which one gets sacrificed when the alarm goes off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer the invitation next to an easy excuse.
beats.text: Pick the comfort of staying home or the chance you say you want.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is waiting your choice, or the sentence your fear prefers?

D107.title: Stay for the Hard Part
D107.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave a little more of the difficult letter exposed.
beats.text: Can you stay with me while I say one less comfortable thing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know if I can hear this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can say that. Could you stay while I read just this next line?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move from the small admission to the next line.
beats.text: Listen to the harder part before deciding we're finished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought that was everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It was the part I could say first. Let me try one more.

D108.title: Drop the Armor
D108.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set the ceremonial brave face mask aside.
beats.text: You can put down the strong voice here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave fine on the table for a minute. What needed the mask?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a plain cup instead of a toast.
beats.text: Tell me one thing that actually got to you today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't have anything worth complaining about.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me one small thing without proving it was large enough.

D109.title: I Started the Spiral
D109.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hide the panicked message I sent first.
beats.text: Let's calm everyone down without tracing who raised the alarm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You called everyone at midnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now I'm available to reassure all of them. Very efficient.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I wipe my name from the worry list.
beats.text: We can solve this by focusing on the present, not my earlier calls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your handwriting is on every warning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which means I know exactly where to start calming things down.

D110.title: Not the Real Fear
D110.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I count teaspoons beside the unopened results.
beats.text: Before the frightening part, do we have enough clean spoons?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter won't read itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, and tea won't stir itself. One solvable problem at a time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I check the departure time repeatedly.
beats.text: Let's settle the timetable instead of discussing what scares me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're checking that again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can understand the train. Let me stay with the train a little longer.

D111.title: Let Them Keep Hope
D111.instruction: Hide discouraging information because you believe hope is the only thing keeping someone able to continue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tuck the discouraging result beneath the plan.
beats.text: There is still something worth trying this morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What does the bottom number say?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The top line leaves us a possibility. Let's make breakfast for that possibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I underline a small possibility, hiding the worse number.
beats.text: Look at the one thing that hasn't ruled us out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You covered most of the page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So we can see the one part that still needs our effort.

D112.title: Admit You’re Hurt
D112.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I keep my crumpled note under the table.
beats.text: Were you disappointed too, or was that only how it looked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why? Were you upset?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I noticed your face first. Tell me about yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer the tissue box without taking one.
beats.text: Tell me what hurt you before I explain why I brought tissues.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You look like you need one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm very well stocked. Which part got to you?

D113.title: A Necessary Heartbreak
D113.instruction: Describe disappointment, rejection, or loss as the exact experience everyone needed in order to grow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I label the rejected invitation 'growth'.
beats.text: This disappointment is exactly the lesson we needed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It just hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but think of the emotional vocabulary we're gaining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the broken keepsake in a new box.
beats.text: Losing it this way makes room for something truer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather have the old thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. That's why this lesson has such a convincing beginning.

D114.title: I Can Handle This
D114.instruction: Perform complete emotional readiness while quietly borrowing coping strategies from every response around you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I copy the calming breath while claiming composure.
beats.text: Yes, that breathing method is part of how I handle things.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You just copied my breath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's called synchronizing. I was establishing the rhythm.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I follow a suggested step as though it was my plan.
beats.text: Water first, obviously; I was just reaching for it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said water wouldn't help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not without the right timing. Now the timing is excellent.

D115.title: Outfeel the Room
D115.instruction: Answer every fear, sacrifice, or disappointment with one of your own that deserves more attention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add a heavier folder to the worries on the table.
beats.text: That's difficult; wait until you hear what I'm carrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This isn't a contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it won't matter if my pile happens to be larger.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I count my sleepless nights on more fingers.
beats.text: One rough night? Let me put that in perspective.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only wanted to tell you about mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now you'll have a properly calibrated scale.

D116.title: Hope Keeps Moving
D116.instruction: Turn every disappointment into a new reason the desired outcome is delayed, redirected, or becoming more meaningful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the hoped-for date farther along the calendar.
beats.text: Not this Friday means more time for the right answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They said no.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They said no on Friday. Saturday hasn't spoken yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw a new route around the failed one.
beats.text: It isn't gone; the hope has changed its address.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's another dead end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We've narrowed down where the answer isn't.

D117.title: Comfort Everyone Else
D117.instruction: Meet every painful moment by comforting someone else more intensely while your own distress becomes harder to hide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hand out tissues while hiding my wet sleeve.
beats.text: Let's make sure you're all right before anybody checks on me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your sleeve is wet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A spill. Tell me what happened to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pour another comforting drink without taking my own.
beats.text: Tell me your trouble; mine can keep standing in the kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: When did you last sit down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once everyone has a cup, sitting will make more sense.

D118.title: Emotional Interest
D118.instruction: Treat comfort, vulnerability, and forgiveness as investments that must eventually be repaid with equal emotional risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I write a quiet promise beside the comfort I offered.
beats.text: I'll carry this with you; someday I need you equally unguarded.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you help without keeping score?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can. I'm asking whether someday you could meet me here too.

examples.transferProp: the written promise beside the tea

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I exchange my folded confession for an empty page.
beats.text: I've risked my truth; meet me with one of yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't have to tell me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I chose to. I'd like to know we're risking something together.

D119.title: Ready on My Terms
D119.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I mark one safe subject on the confession list.
beats.text: I'll be honest about this part and keep the rest closed today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more to this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There is. Today I can finish this one sentence without running.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I choose the chair nearest the exit.
beats.text: Yes to talking, provided I can pause whenever I need to.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you already planning to leave?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Knowing I can leave is what's letting me sit down.

D120.title: The Same Ending
D120.instruction: Use every new emotional detail as evidence that the same feared ending is becoming inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I circle the same ominous phrase in a new letter.
beats.text: That word again; this is heading toward the ending I feared.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't say it's over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It uses the same comma as the last goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move a new disappointment beside the old photograph.
beats.text: It's happening in the same order, only faster this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This is a different person.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why am I putting the cups away in the same order?

D121.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
D121.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide the sealed envelope under a tray.
beats.text: Help me keep this out of sight before asking what's in it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What am I hiding?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Something you'll find easier to explain after it's out of sight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a key to an unexplained cupboard.
beats.text: Hold this until tomorrow and don't mention the cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why can't I mention it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because a cupboard becomes much more interesting once people know there's a key.

D122.title: Not Until You Explain
D122.instruction: Keep someone present until they account for one contradiction, omission, or suspicious change in their story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put two contradictory departure times together.
beats.text: Before you leave, explain the hour that appears in only one account.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have to catch my bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then explain the missing hour in the time we have before it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the changed note beside a coat.
beats.text: Wait until you've explained why this line was altered.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can talk tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The line changed tonight. I need tonight's explanation.

D123.title: Apologize for the Lie
D123.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that the concealment or misdirection mattered, even if the underlying choice was defensible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I uncover the part of the message that was hidden.
beats.text: Apologize for keeping me in the dark, not for the decision itself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was protecting you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologize for deciding I couldn't hear it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place the public version next to the private one.
beats.text: Acknowledge that telling me half the truth changed everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You got the main facts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you kept the fact that would have changed my answer.

D124.title: Approve the Cover Story
D124.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I rehearse the cover story from a small card.
beats.text: Agree that we were collecting chairs, not opening the cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: But we did open the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only between collecting chairs. Let's emphasize the chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pass over the harmless version of the timetable.
beats.text: Back this explanation if anyone asks about the missing hour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if they ask about that hour?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll agree now that it was a very slow journey.

D125.title: You Handle the Evidence
D125.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold out the box with the revealing label.
beats.text: You look after the evidence; I'll handle the less dangerous details.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your name is on the label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why your cupboard would be a much safer location.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I slide the follow-up call list across.
beats.text: Take responsibility for explaining the loose end nobody can ignore.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why should I explain your loose end?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have a reassuring voice. Mine keeps sounding personally involved.

D126.title: What Really Happened?
D126.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I arrange three versions of the story by time.
beats.text: Tell it again starting before the missing ten minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already told you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the next version should match one of these.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to a changed noun in two accounts.
beats.text: Which object was actually there, the bag or the box?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It might have been a bag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles before deciding what to call it.

D127.title: Back My Version
D127.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I write a simple shared account on two cards.
beats.text: Remember this version with me: we arrived after the lights went out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I arrived before the lights went out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not in the version we're rehearsing together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pass over the words I'd like repeated.
beats.text: Back my explanation when they ask about the extra key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Do I have to say those exact words?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only until they stop asking the question.

D128.title: Test the Story First
D128.instruction: Get someone else to repeat the explanation, ask the dangerous question, or test the risky step before you commit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I give you the rehearsal account without signing mine.
beats.text: Try that explanation on the first person who asks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Won't they recognize your handwriting?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read it aloud. I'm testing the explanation, not the paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point toward the person with the awkward answer.
beats.text: Ask the risky question first; I'll hear how it lands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you coming with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll be close enough to hear whether it's safe to join in.

D129.title: Credit for the Discovery
D129.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you found the clue, saw through the deception, or designed the successful scheme.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I circle my initials beside the earliest clue.
beats.text: Say who discovered this before the discovery becomes everyone's.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The discovery belongs to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Its arrival time belongs beside my name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I bring my original sketch out of the drawer.
beats.text: Mention that my diagram found the hidden door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We all looked at it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I drew the door while it was still a wall.

D130.title: Truth or Loyalty
D130.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put a private letter beside our photograph.
beats.text: Choose whether to answer that question or keep this confidence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why can't I do both?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The answer is in the letter. Our promise is beside it. Pick up one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold the revealing page above the public pile.
beats.text: Decide which matters now: the complete truth or protecting us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They deserve the truth.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say what becomes of the confidence when you hand it over.

D131.title: Can You Keep It?
D131.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a mild secret and watch the doorway.
beats.text: Keep this small detail quiet before I tell you the important one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't tell anyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who is the first person you'll be tempted not to tell?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I start a more sensitive sentence and pause.
beats.text: Where would these words go after I leave the room?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can trust me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where would you put the sentence if somebody asked nicely?

D132.title: Hand Over the Proof
D132.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold out an empty evidence envelope.
beats.text: Give me the original note, not your description of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can tell you what's in the note.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your telling is what I'm trying to check against the paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the locked drawer.
beats.text: Hand over the key that lets me check the actual proof.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those are private records.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me the exact page, not your summary of the drawer.

D133.title: Steer the Suspicion
D133.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place a safer explanation over the clue to my mistake.
beats.text: That stain could be from the delivery; let's follow that first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You accepted the delivery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I can point us toward the person who packed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn my marked tool so the brand is hidden.
beats.text: Look at the faulty shelf, not who last tightened it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the wrench you borrowed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: From a shelf that clearly needs investigating.

D134.title: Anything but That Question
D134.instruction: Redirect every attempt to discuss the one detail that could expose your real motive or involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tap an unrelated time on the schedule.
beats.text: We'll get to why I had the key; first, when does the bus leave?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why did you have the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If we miss the bus, everyone will be asking a much larger question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I display the least revealing photograph.
beats.text: Let's talk about this angle instead of the person just outside it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who's standing just outside the frame?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sun was in that direction. Notice what it does to the colours.

D135.title: A Kinder Version
D135.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I read only the gentler half of the letter.
beats.text: They said the event changed; you don't need every unkind sentence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me read the rest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The rest changes how much it hurts, not what we need to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the harsh original under my shortened note.
beats.text: Here's the version that tells you what to do next, not what hurts most.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: These aren't their exact words.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. They're the words you can get through breakfast with.

D136.title: Tell Me Why
D136.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I reveal a small piece of my private note.
beats.text: I changed my mind once too; what made you choose that door?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why are you telling me that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So you know I understand choosing a door for the wrong reason.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I admit one harmless fear and leave room for yours.
beats.text: I was afraid of being excluded; why did you hide the invitation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you'd be angry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I was frightened of being left out. What were you frightened of?

D137.title: Exactly as Planned
D137.instruction: Treat every exposed flaw, failed step, and unexpected consequence as proof that the scheme is unfolding by design.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I tick a failure as though it were a planned stage.
beats.text: The exposed flaw means the first phase is working.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was the flaw we meant to prevent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before anyone knew to look for it. Now we're ahead of expectations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn the spoiled diagram toward the next arrow.
beats.text: Exactly as designed: now nobody expects the original plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The plan is ruined.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The recognizable plan. The unrecognizable phase is proceeding beautifully.

D138.title: I Know the Procedure
D138.instruction: Perform investigative confidence while quietly using each response to discover what the questions, clues, and next steps should be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn a new answer into my next confident question.
beats.text: Yes, the second key was the next thing I meant to examine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't know there was a second key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I was waiting to see whether you'd identify it independently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I copy a useful term into my investigative notes.
beats.text: Naturally, we test the hinge discrepancy before proceeding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just invented that term.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A useful test of whether I'd recognize a new formulation.

D139.title: Outsmart the Room
D139.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I claim a new clue with my pencil before looking at it.
beats.text: I'll solve that before anyone else finishes reading it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't read it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm reserving the answer while I work out the details.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put my deduction above the other notes.
beats.text: Compare your answer with mine after I've named it first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We came to the same conclusion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then check whose pencil arrived first.

D140.title: The Plan Gets Better
D140.instruction: Celebrate every setback as proof that the scheme is becoming more sophisticated, selective, or impossible to detect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I celebrate a hole appearing in the cover story.
beats.text: Excellent, a plan this complicated will be impossible to copy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They don't believe any of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. They can't predict which part we'll improve next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add another detour to the map.
beats.text: Every setback makes our route harder to predict.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've lost our route.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So has anyone following us. That's a strategic tie.

D141.title: Warmly Withholding
D141.instruction: Remain open, caring, and reassuring while revealing less with every new question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer a warm cup while closing another folder.
beats.text: I'm glad you asked; let's leave that part safely tucked away.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You still haven't answered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have made sure you have something warm while waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I smile and reduce a detailed answer to one word.
beats.text: Everything is fine; the longer version would only worry you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine isn't an explanation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But notice how comfortably it fits into the conversation.

D142.title: Secrets Have Value
D142.instruction: Price every fact, introduction, warning, and confession as something that must be traded for equal value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold a clue beside an empty IOU.
beats.text: One useful name costs one useful truth from you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You already know the answer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which saves you the uncertainty of what you're buying.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I divide my confession into pieces on the table.
beats.text: Trade me a warning and I'll trade you the next detail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want payment for being honest?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the next installment. The first sentence was complimentary.

D143.title: I Told You Enough
D143.instruction: Agree to be honest while repeatedly narrowing what honesty requires and which details count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the single question I answered.
beats.text: I said where I was, not what I carried.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So you did take the box?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now that's a different question, and beautifully specific.

examples.transferProp: the question with its answer crossed out

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cross out 'complete account' and write 'honest answers'.
beats.text: Honesty means answering what you actually asked, nothing more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's not a complete account.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It is a complete answer to the incomplete question you asked.

D144.title: The Conspiracy Expands
D144.instruction: Use every denial, coincidence, and missing detail as proof that more people and higher stakes are involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I connect a missing receipt to three more names.
beats.text: The missing paper proves somebody else is helping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Maybe it fell out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A disappearance with no witnesses. The helpers are getting careful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I mark a denial as a new link.
beats.text: That confident no is exactly what a larger operation would need.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you nobody else was involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Such a coordinated refusal to name anyone is useful evidence.

D145.title: Help Me Make This Normal
D145.instruction: Get someone to help perform the strange behavior until it feels ordinary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set a place for the talking cupboard.
beats.text: Pass it a napkin with me like this happens every dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cupboard doesn't eat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then pass the napkin for its lap. We needn't make it uncomfortable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I demonstrate a casual greeting to the empty chair.
beats.text: Help me welcome the invisible guest without making it a spectacle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't see anyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Look at the chair when you say hello. That's how we'd welcome a visible guest.

D146.title: You Can’t Leave Mid-Prophecy
D146.instruction: Keep someone present until the impossible prediction has been fulfilled, disproved, or responsibly revised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold the prophecy beside the unused coat hook.
beats.text: Wait until the predicted visitor appears or we responsibly revise this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody is coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we should stay to discover what visitor means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I pencil another possible meaning under the prediction.
beats.text: We can't leave while 'before sunset' still has interpretations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sun has already set.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here. There are other time zones we should responsibly consider.

D147.title: Apologize to Reality
D147.instruction: Get someone to apologize to an object, rule, place, or idea for violating its impossible expectations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer an apology card to a chair.
beats.text: Say sorry to the chair for sitting before it agreed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then a short apology will cost you very little dignity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to the insulted doorway.
beats.text: Apologize to the doorway before asking it to open again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Doors don't hold grudges.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Yours should be accepted immediately.

D148.title: Approve the Impossible Plan
D148.instruction: Get someone to formally approve a plan whose logic becomes stranger each time it is explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I lay out a plan for borrowing tomorrow's weather.
beats.text: Approve the first step: we'll store Tuesday's rain in this cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tuesday hasn't happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why the storage cup is currently empty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw a staircase up to a missing floor.
beats.text: Sign off on the invisible landing before we build the stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's nothing to sign off on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Approving it now avoids later visible objections.

D149.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
D149.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I assign the impossible section of a simple list.
beats.text: You fold the moon; I'll stack the chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How am I supposed to fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the crescent. It already has a crease.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hand over a jar labelled 'yesterday'.
beats.text: Put the missing hour back in here before lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't put time in a jar.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then use the lid first so we don't lose any more.

D150.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
D150.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I list ordinary rules beside the floating bowl.
beats.text: Which rule keeps the soup inside when the bowl turns upside down?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've never seen this either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We can test which direction counts as down for the soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I mark the moment the shadow stopped following.
beats.text: What changed just before the shadow decided to lead?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Maybe we're moving slowly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stop completely. Let's find out whether the shadow gets bored.

D151.title: Believe This with Me
D151.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I place my impossible diagram between our cups.
beats.text: Work with me as though the house really is migrating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Houses don't migrate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This one packed the chimney. Help me plan where it rests.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I draw a plan around the talking kettle.
beats.text: Accept its complaints as advice and help me respond.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only says boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A clear agenda. Let's ask what it's prepared to contribute.

D152.title: Test the Impossible Claim
D152.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I offer an empty cup beneath a cloud drawing.
beats.text: Try catching one drop of tomorrow before I stake my plan on it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You catch tomorrow first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone needs to remain in today to record the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point at the supposedly invisible bridge.
beats.text: Test the first step with your umbrella before I walk across.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why my umbrella?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It has a longer reach and fewer dependants.

D153.title: Credit for the Impossible
D153.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you understood, predicted, or accepted the impossible truth before anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I display an old sketch of today's impossible event.
beats.text: Remember who drew the floating staircase before it appeared.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can all see it now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but I drew the handrail while everyone was calling me mistaken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn my earlier note toward the light.
beats.text: Credit me for believing the cupboard before it started talking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's asking us for silence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'd like it to mention who listened before it learned to speak.

D154.title: Choose the Real Impossibility
D154.instruction: Make someone choose which of two incompatible explanations will govern what everyone does next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put two incompatible diagrams side by side.
beats.text: Choose: are we shrinking, or is the room growing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Maybe nothing has changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My trousers disagree. Choose the explanation that tells me which doorway fits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold two rulebooks with opposite arrows.
beats.text: Pick whether gravity is late or we are early, so I can plan lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Neither explanation makes sense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But only one lets us arrive early for lunch. Choose that one explicitly.

D155.title: Act as If It’s True
D155.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put an extra bowl on the high shelf.
beats.text: If the ceiling is hungry, put its breakfast where it can reach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it's not hungry?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll have offered breakfast politely. Put the bowl up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I label a seat for a guest from tomorrow.
beats.text: Reserve that chair as though tomorrow's visitor has already accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody has accepted yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow's guests work ahead. Leave the seat available.

D156.title: Abandon the Normal Explanation
D156.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender the last ordinary explanation and proceed entirely within the stranger one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I put the ordinary repair guide away.
beats.text: Stop calling it faulty wiring and start asking the house what it wants.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's obviously an electrical fault.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask the house whether it prefers the hall light on. Listen before resetting it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cross out 'lost' and write 'invisible'.
beats.text: Leave the missing-key explanation behind and search without your eyes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to see where I'm looking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Close your eyes and listen for the keyring. Try the new explanation once.

D157.title: I Started the Weirdness
D157.instruction: Hide that one casual choice caused the impossible situation while eagerly helping manage each new consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hide the switch I flipped beside the floating cups.
beats.text: Let's manage the levitation without discussing that little switch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That switch has your fingerprint on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course I checked it. Now somebody needs to tether the cups.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I cover my handwriting on the summoning label.
beats.text: The important thing is feeding it, not who wrote its name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This is your handwriting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I can read the feeding instructions particularly well.

D158.title: Don’t Question the Premise
D158.instruction: Redirect every attempt to ask why the strange situation exists toward what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn from the impossible apparition to a shopping list.
beats.text: We can ask why it exists later; what do we feed it now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is there a ghost here?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll get to that after finding out whether it eats the expensive cereal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I set out a bucket beneath the miracle.
beats.text: Stop debating the premise long enough to catch the dripping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: But how can it be happening?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bucket doesn't need the explanation to fill up.

D159.title: Keep Hope Operational
D159.instruction: Protect their hope with practical evidence and next steps while quietly withholding what makes the impossible outcome unlikely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I move the discouraging calculation under the next-step list.
beats.text: We can still prepare its welcome while we wait for proof.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The numbers say it can't arrive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The spare chair won't hurt anybody while we wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I display a tiny workable experiment.
beats.text: Look at this small success before reading the impossible odds.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That isn't proof the big version works.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It is enough proof to keep the next small step on the table.

D160.title: Say You Saw It Too
D160.instruction: Get someone to admit noticing the impossible detail before you reveal how much you believe it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I leave my own strange observation unspoken.
beats.text: Did you notice the shadow moving before the chair moved?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What did you see?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd rather hear where you thought it went before I influence you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I point to an empty bowl without explaining.
beats.text: Tell me whether the soup just waved at you too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're staring at the bowl.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm waiting to discover whether we're remembering the same gesture.

D161.title: Failure Reveals the Mission
D161.instruction: Use each failed step to reveal a different goal the plan was secretly pursuing, then act immediately on that new mission.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I turn a failed map toward a different destination.
beats.text: We weren't meant to find the door; we were meant to wake the wall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So the map was wrong?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only about the destination. Waking the wall was the real discovery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I use the broken instrument for a new purpose.
beats.text: The failed signal proves our real mission is to listen, not transmit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's not sending anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. We were meant to hear what was already calling us.

D162.title: Fluent in Nonsense
D162.instruction: Perform complete mastery of the strange logic while inventing each rule only when it becomes necessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I invent a measuring gesture over the invisible guest.
beats.text: Naturally, you count the third elbow when measuring a cloud.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Clouds don't have elbows.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not the first two. The third is what distinguishes professional measurement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I correct the imaginary dial with certainty.
beats.text: That's basic reversed gravity; the next rule will explain it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where did you learn that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Advanced training. Its first rule arrives after you use the second.

D163.title: Raise the Impossibility
D163.instruction: Answer every strange offer with a more committed version that you can still justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I add another chair above the floating one.
beats.text: A flying chair needs a flying table, not a nervous audience.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One flying chair is quite enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For sitting. Where do you expect it to eat without a flying table?

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I address an invisible guest's invisible entourage.
beats.text: One unseen visitor? Let's set the whole banquet for them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We only invited one guest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leaving the invisible entourage hungry would be unforgivably visible hospitality.

D164.title: Every Glitch Is a Gift
D164.instruction: Turn every contradiction or failure into a surprising benefit of the impossible system.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I applaud the door opening into the wrong room.
beats.text: Perfect, we've removed the commute between mistakes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're in the broom cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. We can clean up this mistake without travelling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I use the backwards clock to excuse the delay.
beats.text: Wonderful, late now means we're early yesterday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: But we missed the meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tomorrow we'll arrive before the invitation existed.

D165.title: Calm About the Impossible
D165.instruction: Remain perfectly calm around impossible events while becoming increasingly alarmed by ordinary details.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I calmly feed the invisible creature and inspect the carpet.
beats.text: Its three heads are fine; the crumbs are becoming unacceptable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're worried about crumbs, not three heads?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three heads can learn to use one napkin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I ignore a floating table to check a small stain.
beats.text: Levitation I understand; who put a wet cup directly on the wood?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The table is flying.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, and carrying a water ring to every altitude.

D166.title: Impossible Currency
D166.instruction: Price every favor in symbolic acts, imaginary resources, or promises that cannot be measured normally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I hold out an empty jar as payment.
beats.text: I'll help for two unspoken promises and a spoonful of yesterday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I give you yesterday?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the five minutes you wasted this morning. We'll work backward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.action: I weigh an imaginary coin on my palm.
beats.text: One favour costs a borrowed shadow until Friday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need my shadow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then return my ladder on Friday and we'll reunite you.

D167.title: Yes, Under My Physics
